# INDIAMART — Investment Dossier (2026-08-14)

IndiaMART InterMESH Limited runs India's largest online business-to-business marketplace: about 220,000 paying suppliers pay subscription fees (Silver/Gold/Platinum tiers) to be found by buyers who search for free, plus a smaller consolidated accounting-software subsidiary (Busy Infotech).

# PART I — INVESTMENT COMMITTEE DECISION

## 1. One-Line Decision

**Decision: Watchlist — the market is not clearly wrong about IndiaMART's price, and this engine's own valuation base case (₹1,699/share) sits below today's ₹1,784.60, so there is no cushion to buy today; the trend to track before acting is whether paying-supplier net additions turn positive over the next 1–2 quarters.**

## 3. Would I Buy This With Real Money Today?

**Final answer: I would not buy this today because the price already sits above this engine's own triangulated fair value (₹1,699 base case vs. ₹1,784.60 today, a −5.0% margin of safety — meaning there is no discount to close), and the single biggest swing factor (whether paying-supplier net additions turn positive) is unresolved and management itself has given no firm timeline beyond "2, 3 more quarters."**

- **Confidence score:** Conviction 58/100 (non-committal — Watchlist decisions are capped in the upper "toss-up" band by design, since a neutral rating should not carry buy-level conviction). Understanding 75.5/100 (the situation is well evidenced — six modules ran, four with "Sufficient" data triage and no active partial-data caps).
- **Position stance:** No position. This is not a rejection of the company (fortress balance sheet, real cash generation, founder-aligned ownership) — it is a rejection of the *price* given the unresolved demand question.
- **What would raise confidence:** Two consecutive quarters of non-negative paying-supplier net adds while EBITDA margin holds near 33–35% as acquisition spend resumes on schedule (proves the margin tailwind and demand drag are genuinely independent, not the same problem); a resolved, low-end beta estimate that lifts the DCF base case materially above today's price; a disclosed tier-level retention/NRR figure showing Gold/Platinum durably insulated from the Silver-tier price pushback.
- **What would lower confidence:** A 4th consecutive quarter of negative net adds; acquisition spend resuming to the guided ~₹10cr/quarter run-rate while net adds are still negative (the named compounding-bear scenario); a further high-vote-against related-party resolution at the FY27 AGM, echoing the 21.72%-against Amit Agarwal vote.
- **What would force exit/rejection (from a hypothetical position):** Confirmation that the compounding-bear scenario is playing out (revenue and margin miss together); a material write-up/scale-up of the newly incorporated lending subsidiary (IndiaMART Finance Limited) that turns a stated partnership-lending model into on-balance-sheet credit risk; a repeat FY27 pay-for-performance divergence (CEO pay up, EPS/price down).

## 4. The Actual Variant Perception

- **What everyone already knows:** Revenue growth has decelerated every year since FY23 (30.8% → 13.0% FY26 → 11.4% YoY in the latest quarter, the softest of the last 8); paying-supplier net additions have been negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters; management said on the Q1 FY27 call that buyer growth is stagnating; sell-side target-price revisions are 16 down vs. 1 up of 18 analysts over 3 months, and the average recommendation has drifted from Outperform to Hold.
- **What is probably priced in:** Per the reverse-DCF, today's price implies only a ~6.0% flat revenue CAGR over the next 8 years — below every year of the company's actual growth in the last 5 years — so the market has already discounted a real slowdown. It has not, however, discounted the *specific* compounding scenario below.
- **What the engine thinks may be missed:** The Q1 FY27 35.35% EBITDA margin is a management-labelled *temporary* policy choice (deferred acquisition spend), not a new baseline, and management itself said it plans to hold that stance for roughly "2, 3 more quarters." If subscriber net adds have not turned by then, revenue and margin miss together — not two offsetting forces, but the same underlying SME-demand weakness expressed twice (earnings module, Critical flag). The sell-side mean target (₹2,093.72, +17.3% implied upside) has not caught up to this mechanism; this engine's own triangulated base case (₹1,699, −4.8%) and bear case (₹1,229, −31.1%) sit materially below it.
- **What evidence would prove we are actually different:** If, over the next two reported quarters (Q2 FY27 ~21-Oct-2026, Q3 FY27 ~Jan-2027), paying-supplier net adds turn and stay positive for 2 consecutive quarters *while* EBITDA margin holds at or above ~33–34% as acquisition spend resumes on schedule, this engine's bear-leaning read is wrong and the Street's optimism is closer to correct. If net adds instead stay negative through that window while spend is forced to resume, the compounding-bear read is confirmed.

**Edge score: 55/100 (Moderate).** This is not restated consensus — the engine's own base/bear case sits below the sell-side mean target, a genuine, evidenced divergence — but it rests on primary evidence (management's own admissions and guidance walk-downs) rather than a proprietary data source, so it does not clear the bar for a high-conviction edge. `edge_proof` is stated above and is checkable at the Q2/Q3 FY27 prints.

## 5. Thesis → Antithesis → Final Thesis

- **Thesis:** IndiaMART is a debt-free, cash-generative subscription marketplace with a real (if narrow) moat, currently priced for only conservative growth — a reasonable long at today's price.
- **Antithesis:** The subscription engine that funds the cash generation is under simultaneous strain on both sides — buyer growth stagnating, supplier net adds negative in 3 of 4 quarters — and the margin cushion masking that strain is management-labelled temporary. The price is not cheap on this engine's own triangulated fair value (−5.0% margin of safety), and the one clean peer comp (Just Dial) argues the current P/E premium is not fully earned.
- **Revised thesis:** The balance sheet removes solvency risk entirely (Fortress verdict, no break point even past a 100% EBITDA decline), so the downside is bounded by business risk, not financial risk — this is a "wait for a better price or a resolving data point" situation, not an "avoid" situation.
- **Antithesis:** Waiting has a real cost if the bull case is right — the reverse-DCF shows the market's growth bar is unusually low, and a confirmed net-add turn could re-rate the stock toward the bull case (+28.8%) quickly, since 25% of this thesis's own probability mass sits in that outcome.
- **Final thesis:** Hold at Watchlist. The name deserves close tracking, not ownership, until the single swing variable (subscriber net adds) resolves in one direction or the price falls enough to restore a margin of safety. This is a monitoring position, not a conviction call in either direction.
- **Insight threshold reached:** the remaining uncertainty is mostly data-dependent, not reasoning-dependent — the next 1–2 quarterly prints, not further analysis of the current pool, will resolve most of the open question.

## 6. Simple Summary

- IndiaMART runs India's biggest online marketplace connecting buyers (who search free) with paying suppliers (about 220,000 of them, paying subscription fees).
- It could go up because the price is not demanding much: the market is pricing in only ~6% yearly revenue growth for the next 8 years, well below the company's own recent growth, and the balance sheet has zero real debt with ~₹31 billion of net cash.
- It could go down because the number of paying customers has been shrinking for three of the last four quarters, management itself said buyer growth is stagnating, and the healthy-looking profit margin right now is a temporary choice (deferred marketing spend) management says will end in a couple of quarters.
- The data supporting this: six research modules ran, most with "Sufficient" data quality and no active caps — this is a well-evidenced picture, not a thin one.
- What's missing: how many customers the company loses each quarter to cancellation by subscription tier (only the net change is disclosed), and a resolved estimate for the discount rate used in the valuation model (three different vendors give wildly different numbers).
- Buy now or wait: wait. This engine's own fair-value estimate (₹1,699) sits below today's price (₹1,784.60) — there's no discount to buy at.
- The one next thing to check: the Q2 FY27 results, expected around 21-Oct-2026 — specifically whether the number of paying suppliers stopped shrinking.

## Sign Check (Step 3b)

The single driver this thesis turns on is: **SME/paying-supplier demand stays soft (a headwind read on the marketplace's core growth engine).** The module that owns this variable is `earnings` (via `02_revenue-drivers`, `05_beat-miss-setup`, `08_earnings-red-flags`). Its own synthesis (`99_earnings-synthesis.md`) reads: *"Mixed earnings setup"*, escalated from the sub-agent's "Balanced" framing specifically *because* the red-flags specialist assessed the demand/margin interaction as **Critical**. This thesis's cautious sign matches the module's own most-conservative, most-recent read — there is no inversion here to defend. `business-model`'s synthesis independently reaches the same sign ("Average business — worth deeper work only if valuation is cheap," and valuation says it is not cheap), and `valuation`'s own synthesis independently lands the base case below today's price. All three owning modules agree with the thesis's direction; no override of a specialist was required.

## 6. Valuation and Peer Mispricing

*Defers to `analyses/INDIAMART_2026-08-14/valuation/99_valuation-synthesis.md`.*

**Verdict: Fairly valued.** Base-case fair value ≈ ₹1,699/share, about 5% *below* today's ₹1,784.60 close (2026-08-12, pool-verified) — there is no cushion. Bull ₹2,298 (+28.8%) / Base ₹1,699 (−4.8%) / Bear ₹1,229 (−31.1% downside-to-bear). The dominant method is the intrinsic DCF (70% weight, full audited 8-year FCFF build with executed consistency checks), cross-checked by a reverse-DCF showing the price implies only a conservative ~6.0% flat revenue CAGR over 8 years. The peer method (30% weight) is the one credible cross-section (P/E vs. Just Dial), finding IndiaMART trades at an 87.9% premium its quality edge does not fully earn.

The valuation module's single biggest fragility is the cost-of-equity beta: three data vendors disagree by 4x (0.24 to 0.91), and at the "conventional beta" WACC of 13.0%, the identical DCF produces ₹1,701/share — below today's price either way. No growth or margin assumption in the model moves the answer nearly as much.

**RF-OWN-004 correction.** The valuation module's own text states the management-governance module "does not exist in this run root" and defers its unaligned-owner (§24 Filter 6) check to the master synthesizer. This is stale: the management-governance module IS present in this run root (carried forward from 2026-08-13), and its row `04-013` explicitly finds **RF-OWN-004 not triggered** — IndiaMART is a standalone, founder-operated company, not government-controlled, not a listed subsidiary of a value-maximizing-elsewhere parent, and not a sprawling unrelated-diversified conglomerate. This clears the valuation module's own open question: the ~31% EV/EBITDA de-rating is **not** an unaligned-owner value trap. ## 8. Scenario Model

| Case | Probability | Return | Price Target | What Must Happen |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Bull | 25% | +28.8% | ₹2,298 | Acquisition opex stays deferred; ARPU keeps compounding ~8%/yr; Busy Infotech sustains ~43% billing growth with improving margin; EV/EBITDA multiple expands as the negative-net-add trend visibly reverses — a 4-condition conjunction tied to one underlying variable (SME demand turning favourable) |

Probabilities sum to 100%. Fair-value levels are the valuation module's (`valuation/07_scenario-and-fair-value.md` §3); the probabilities are this synthesis's own judgment, weighted toward Base/Bear given the earnings module's Critical flag and the valuation module's own bear-leaning DCF sensitivity.

**Correlated-scenario / joint-tail check.** All three cases turn on essentially **one variable**: whether SME/paying-supplier demand recovers, and whether management can hold off resuming acquisition spend while it does. This is not a diversified spread of independent risks — bull and bear are mirror images of the same underlying question resolving in opposite directions. The bear case does not coincide with any solvency stress (the balance sheet survives every channel tested even past a 100% EBITDA decline), so there is no compounded "business risk + balance-sheet risk" tail here — the downside is bounded to the operating business, not amplified by leverage.

**Span check:** the bull case (+28.8%) and bear case (−31.1%) both sit well outside a single ordinary weekly move for this stock (52-week range ₹1,730–₹2,685, a ~55% range) — the scenario set is not artificially narrow. **Conjunction check:** the bull case requires four conditions that this synthesis explicitly ties to one common driver (see `joint_probability_basis` in `decision_record.json`), consistent with `CLAUDE.md` §10's requirement not to treat a multi-condition case as if it were four independent, multiplicatively-improbable events.

Math (executed, see §14 for the reconciled figures):

- Probability-weighted expected return: **−4.31%**
- Probability-weighted target price: **₹1,707.75**
- Main upside driver: net-add reversal + retained margin discipline
- Main downside driver: the compounding-bear scenario (spend resumes while demand stays soft)
- Risk/reward: **−0.14** (negative — the probability-weighted target sits below today's price, so the expected payoff does not compensate for the bear-case loss)
- **Is the expected return worth the risk? No.** A negative expected return and negative risk/reward, at any reasonable reweighting of these three probabilities (tested at 30/45/25, 20/45/35, and 33/34/33 splits — all three remain negative, see §14), argue against a long position today.

## 11. Positioning and Trade Construction

- **Stance:** No position today. If a position is later warranted (a confirmed net-add turn, or price falling to/below the ₹1,699 base case), start with a starter position, not a full one, given the unresolved beta/valuation fragility.
- **Entry style:** Wait for either (a) a confirmed net-add inflection at the Q2 or Q3 FY27 print, or (b) the price falling to within a few percent of the ₹1,699 base fair value, restoring a genuine margin of safety.
- **Add levels:** Only after 2 consecutive quarters of non-negative net adds with margin holding — not on a single quarter's print.
- **Stop-loss logic:** Not applicable to a monitoring-only stance. If a position is later taken, a stop below the bear case (₹1,229) would need to tolerate a full 31% adverse move before triggering, given the wide own-history band and thin daily liquidity signals in the peer/vendor data reviewed here — **the stop may not protect a position through an earnings-gap move at the Q2 FY27 print (~21-Oct-2026), where the compounding-bear or bull scenario could resolve in a single session.**
- **What not to do:** Do not treat the Busy Infotech 27–30% CAGR growth-rate language or the new IndiaMART Finance Limited subsidiary as bullish catalysts on their own — both are undated, unproven initiatives (§24 Filter 2 pattern) per the catalyst module.
- **Whether to hedge:** Not applicable at a no-position stance.
- **Options vs. stock:** No IBKR options/positioning data exists in this pool for INDIAMART — this cannot be assessed. If options data becomes available, a defined-risk options structure (e.g., a call spread into the Q2 FY27 print) may be preferable to outright stock given the binary-ish nature of the near-term catalyst.

## 12. 2nd Best Bet

**Just Dial Limited** — the one same-country, comparable-scale listed peer with public financials (business-model's named "nearest" comparable with disclosed multiples; TradeIndia, management's own most-cited rival, is private).

- **Why it is #2:** Same underlying theme (India B2B/SME digital lead-generation), but priced at a materially lower multiple (10.29x NTM P/E vs. IndiaMART's implied 13.4x, an 87.9% gap the peer-relative-valuation module finds only partly earned by IndiaMART's quality edge).
- **How it diversifies the main thesis:** A cheaper entry point into the same SME-demand cycle, without paying IndiaMART's full premium for its (currently strained) growth story.
- **Why it may be safer or riskier:** Safer on price paid; riskier on governance — Just Dial has been a subsidiary of Reliance Retail Ventures Limited since October 2021, a parent-controlled structure the management-governance module explicitly excludes as a governance peer for board-independence benchmarking (an unaligned-parent-owner concern of the exact kind §24 Filter 6 flags — though that concern attaches to Just Dial, not to IndiaMART, which this dossier confirms is *not* similarly conflicted). Just Dial also runs lower operating margins (25.3% EBIT vs. IndiaMART's 32.0%).
- **What catalyst would make it better than the main idea:** If IndiaMART's demand-side soft patch is sector-wide rather than company-specific, Just Dial's own paying-customer trend (not reviewed in depth in this pool) would be the cross-check — a sector-wide SME slowdown would argue for neither name; a company-specific IndiaMART problem would argue Just Dial is the safer relative-value play within the same theme.

## 13. Thesis → Antithesis Iteration

### Thesis 1
IndiaMART is a high-quality, debt-free, cash-generative marketplace leader trading at a reasonable price after a real de-rating.

### Antithesis 1
The de-rating reflects genuine deterioration (management-confirmed buyer stagnation, negative net adds in 3 of 4 quarters), not fear alone — the moat is Narrow and its economic-moat test only clears cost of capital on a low-beta assumption.

### Revised Thesis 2
The balance sheet (Fortress, no leverage, no covenant, no break point) means this is a business-risk-only situation — the demand question can be waited out without solvency risk forcing a bad outcome.

### Antithesis 2
Waiting has an opportunity cost, and this engine's own base case (₹1,699) already sits below today's price — there is no valuation cushion rewarding the wait, and the compounding-bear scenario (the Critical earnings flag) means the downside if the wait is wrong is a real 31% loss, not a modest one.

### Final Thesis
Watchlist. The company is fundamentally sound (no solvency risk, real cash generation, aligned founders) but not attractively priced today given an unresolved, management-confirmed demand question. The correct action is to track the next 1–2 quarterly prints for the net-add trend, not to buy or sell today.

**Insight threshold reached: the remaining uncertainty is mostly data-dependent, not reasoning-dependent.**

## 14. Math Validation

Computed with an executed Python script (values copied verbatim into §2, §8, and `decision_record.json` — no independent re-typing):

```
price = 1784.60
bull_target, base_target, bear_target = 2298, 1699, 1229
p_bull, p_base, p_bear = 0.25, 0.45, 0.30   # sums to 1.00 (100%)

r_bull = (2298 - 1784.60) / 1784.60 * 100 = 28.77%
r_base = (1699 - 1784.60) / 1784.60 * 100 = -4.80%
r_bear = (1229 - 1784.60) / 1784.60 * 100 = -31.13%

Expected return = 0.25*28.77 + 0.45*(-4.80) + 0.30*(-31.13) = -4.31%
Probability-weighted target price = 0.25*2298 + 0.45*1699 + 0.30*1229 = ₹1,707.75
Expected return from target = (1707.75 - 1784.60) / 1784.60 * 100 = -4.31%  [reconciles]
Risk/reward = (1707.75 - 1784.60) / (1784.60 - 1229) = -0.14
Downside risk = -min(28.77, -4.80, -31.13) = 31.13%
Margin of safety (base FV basis) = (1699 - 1784.60) / 1699 * 100 = -5.04%
```

- Sum of scenario probabilities: **100%** ✓
- Probability-weighted expected return: **−4.31%**
- Probability-weighted target price: **₹1,707.75**
- Risk/reward: **−0.14**
- Downside risk: **31.13%**
- Margin of safety: **−5.04%** (no cushion; price already sits above the base fair value)

**Sensitivity note:** The negative expected-return/risk-reward conclusion is not an artifact of the specific 25/45/30 weighting chosen — it holds under every reasonable reweighting tested (30/45/25 → −1.31%; 20/45/35 → −7.30%; 33/34/33 equal-weight → −2.41%). All three alternates keep the risk/reward negative. The result is moderately robust to the probability assumption, though it is fully dependent on the valuation module's own fair-value LEVELS, which are themselves dominated by a single fragile input (the DCF's cost-of-equity beta, a 4x vendor dispersion). If that beta resolves toward the low end (0.24–0.44), the base and bull fair-value levels — not the probabilities — would need to be revised upward, which would flip this conclusion.

Math reconciles. No fix required before publishing.

- Single most important catalyst: resolution of core-platform paying-supplier net-add decline over management's own "2, 3 more quarters" window — the swing variable behind both the valuation module's bull and bear cases.
- Biggest bearish catalyst: the compounding-bear scenario across the Q2 FY27–Q1 FY28 prints.
- §24-flagged catalysts (not conviction-lifting): Busy Infotech's 27–30% CAGR target (unproven turnaround, 3 straight years of negative segment EBITDA) and the new IndiaMART Finance Limited subsidiary (undated, unproven-initiative pattern).
- Nothing on the calendar carries a hard, exchange-confirmed date — this drove the catalyst-timing confidence cap applied in this dossier's Confidence Scoring (§ below).

## 17. Consensus Expectations

Capital IQ consensus data is available (18 analysts on Target Price/Recommendation, 15 on Revenue/EBITDA/EPS, dated through 2026-07-14/2026-08-12).

- **Revenue:** FY27E ₹17,201.93mn (NTM ₹17,663.93mn), current-quarter (FQ2 FY27) ₹4,222.5mn.
- **EBITDA:** FY27E ₹5,828.73mn (NTM ₹5,978.7mn), current-quarter ₹1,411.67mn.
- **EPS Normalized:** FY27E ₹92.02 (NTM ₹94.28).
- **Target price:** Mean ₹2,093.72, Median ₹2,066.50, range ₹1,650–2,500 across 18 analysts (Std. Dev. ₹243.48) — implies +17.3% upside from today's ₹1,784.60.
- **Recommendation mix:** 7 Buy, 3 Outperform, 2 Hold, 2 Underperform, 4 Sell — average recommendation Hold (2.61), drifted from Outperform over the prior 6–12 months.
- **Estimate revisions (3 months):** Revenue and EPS revision breadth net negative (−28.6% and −14.3% of 14 analysts); EBITDA breadth net positive (+28.6%); target-price revisions sharply negative (1 up / 16 down of 18 analysts).

**Is the market's bar low, fair, or high?** Fair on revenue (tightly calibrated to actuals for 4 straight quarters) but arguably too high on EPS specifically — FY2027E EPS growth (+16.8%) outpaces FY2027E EBITDA growth (+11.96%) by 4.8pp, plausibly embedding an assumption that the volatile, non-operating treasury-gains line (~30–40% of FY26 PBT/EPS) recurs at similar scale. The sell-side mean target (+17.3% implied upside) has not caught up to the earnings module's own Critical compounding-risk read — this is the crux of this dossier's stated variant perception (§4).

## 18. Balance Sheet and Survival Test

*Defers to `analyses/INDIAMART_2026-08-14/balance-sheet-survival/99_balance-sheet-survival-synthesis.md`.* See Chapter C (Part III) for the full compressed treatment. In plain terms: IndiaMART owes almost nothing (₹216–231mn, all office-lease payments, no bank loans or bonds), has more cash and investments (~₹31 billion) than it could plausibly need, and the stress test shows that even if profit fell all the way to zero, the company would not run into a cash problem. There is no covenant to break because there is nothing borrowed that would come with one. The only real risk to this company runs through its operating business (whether SME customers keep subscribing), not its balance sheet.

## business-model — module synthesis

_Source: `business-model/99_business-model-synthesis.md`_

# Business Model Reality Check — INDIAMART (Synthesis)

## Abstract

IndiaMART runs India's largest online business-to-business marketplace, where 220,000 paying suppliers buy Silver, Gold, or Platinum subscriptions to reach buyers who search for free; the web-marketplace segment supplied 92% of FY26 revenue and nearly all profit. The strongest positive is a debt-free, cash-rich balance sheet: deferred revenue grew 14% in FY26, faster than 9% revenue growth, a positive demand signal. The strongest negative is a two-sided network under strain on both sides: management confirmed buyer growth is stagnating while a Silver-tier price rise pushed net paying-supplier additions negative in three of the last four quarters. No disqualifier fired, but with a narrow moat and mixed business quality, this is an average business worth deeper work only if valuation is cheap.

## 1. First-Pass Verdict

### Automatic Disqualifier Check

| # | Disqualifier | Triggered (Y/N) | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Auditor qualification or going-concern note (last 3 years) | N | Unqualified opinion FY24–FY26, BSR & Co. LLP |
| 2 | >50% promoter / insider shares pledged | N | Promoter & Promoter Group hold 49.17%; no promoter-pledge % disclosed; treated as ~0% |
| 3 | Related-party transactions >25% of revenue or expenses | N | BRSR: purchases 0.72%, sales 0.11% of respective totals (FY26) |
| 4 | Auditor changed twice in last 3 years without disclosed reason | N | Same auditor (BSR & Co. LLP) FY24–FY26, no change |
| 5 | Material restatement (>5% of revenue or net income) in last 2 years | N | No restatement; nearest adjustment (amalgamation-related, ₹70.32m) is ~0.5% of FY25 revenue |
| 6 | Active regulatory enforcement action on financial reporting | N | Only routine indirect-tax (GST/service-tax) disputes under appeal, ₹219.18m contingent liability |
| 7 | >40% of revenue from single customer with no long-term contract | N | No single customer ≥10% of revenue; ~220,000 paying suppliers, structurally dispersed |
| 8 | Negative operating cash flow in 3 of last 4 years (excl. growth-stage) | N | Positive OCF every year FY22–FY26 and LTM Jun-2026 |

No row is Y. The Verdict below is not locked by a disqualifier.

### Verdict

- **Verdict:** Average business — worth deeper work only if valuation is cheap
- Disqualifier triggered: N
- Business clarity /100: 82 — a simple, well-disclosed revenue mechanic (paying suppliers × ARPU, upfront cash collection, deferred revenue as the contract liability), with one real disclosure gap (no quantified retention/churn metric) that keeps it below the top band
- Business quality /100: 55 *(from `07_business-quality.md`, Aggregate: Mixed/Average)*
- Moat /100: 55 *(from `09_moat.md`, strongest moat source — Scale — at 55; overall verdict is Narrow moat)*
- External dependency risk /100 *(higher = worse)*: 52 *(from `10_external-dependency.md`, "Partly externally driven")*
- Capital allocation & governance /100: 74 *(from `11_capital-allocation-governance.md`)*
- Data quality /100: 90 — inferred from `00_data-triage.md`'s "Sufficient" verdict (recent audited annual filing, recent quarterly filing and transcript, ~19 quarters of transcript history, no extraction failures across 85 sources); `00_data-triage.md` itself issues a verdict label, not a numeric score, so this figure is this synthesis's own read of that verdict against the CLAUDE.md §11 bands, not a restated upstream number
- Overall usefulness /100: 58
- Business type (one line): India-focused, subscription-funded B2B online marketplace (classifieds/lead-generation platform) for MSME suppliers, with a smaller consolidated accounting-software subscription subsidiary (Busy Infotech) attached
- Biggest business-model risk (one line): the core subscription-renewal engine depends on a two-sided network where buyer growth has stagnated (management-confirmed, Q1 FY27 call) at the same time supplier-side pricing is being pushed harder, with revenue increasingly concentrated in the top decile of paying suppliers (41% → 49% of revenue, FY21–FY26)

**REJECTOR-FILTER CAPS (CLAUDE.md §24).**
- **Filter 1 — Crooks / integrity.** Not locked. `01_disqualifier-scan.md` found no proven fraud or defrauding of stakeholders — only a soft, self-reported signal (an unnamed Designated Person pledged Company shares without pre-clearance, and a second Designated Person made a one-share trade in a closed window, both self-intimated to the exchanges). This does not clear the hard evidence bar for a lock. It is carried forward as a conviction-capping note, routed to management-governance, not applied as a score cap here.
- **Filter 4 — Serial acquirers.** Not applied. `11_capital-allocation-governance.md` scores the acquisition-pattern row (a ~20-deal history of mostly small minority venture stakes plus one control deal, Busy Infotech) at 58/100 severity — below the ≥70 threshold that would cap Capital Allocation & Governance at 50/100 and Overall usefulness at 70. The pattern is a genuine drag on the governance score (it is why 74/100 is not higher) but does not cross into the debt-funded, near-or-above-company-value territory the cap targets.
- **Filter 5 — Fast-changing industry.** Not applied. `07_business-quality.md` scores the industry rate-of-change / disruption row at 45/100 — inside the Mixed band, not the ≤40 threshold that would cap Business quality at 65 and flag a standalone `RF-BQ-005` tag. No `RF-BQ-005` tag was emitted upstream. The core subscription/lead-generation mechanic is mature; the discovery layer sitting on top of it (AI/agentic search, WhatsApp flows, ONDC) is genuinely in flux and is called out as a monitoring item, not a rejector-filter trip.

**CAPITAL STRUCTURE TRANSACTION CAP.** Not triggered. `11_capital-allocation-governance.md` shows total debt is lease liabilities only (₹216–231m, trivial in absolute size and against ₹5,300m EBITDA) with no debt drawn for any acquisition, and weighted average diluted shares were effectively flat year on year (~60.03m → ~59.96m); neither the >50% debt-change nor the >25% share-count-change trigger condition is met. The Capital allocation & governance score of 74/100 stands uncapped by this rule (it is already discounted for the acquisition pattern, per Filter 4 above).

**Module Disconfirmation (CLAUDE.md §8).**
- **Strongest bear point:** the two-sided network is showing strain on both sides at once — management confirmed on the Q1 FY27 call that "the overall number of buyers are stagnating," while a Silver-tier price increase already turned net paying-supplier additions negative in three of the last four disclosed quarters (Q3 FY26 −1,000, Q4 FY26 −1,200, Q1 FY27 −1,850) [`12_red-flags-sweep.md`; `04_unit-economics.md`].
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** the business is asset-light and self-funding — positive operating cash flow every year FY22–FY26 and LTM, a debt-free balance sheet with roughly ₹31bn of net cash, and a deferred-revenue book growing faster (+14% FY26) than recognized revenue (+9%), which is the cleanest available lead indicator that prepaid demand is still building even as net subscriber adds slow [`01_disqualifier-scan.md`; `02_business-identity.md`; `11_capital-allocation-governance.md`].
- **Single killer risk:** if buyer-side stagnation persists while ARPU keeps being pushed up through Gold/Platinum upsell, the renewal math for the ~75%-of-revenue Gold/Platinum cohort could start behaving like the Silver cohort already has — fewer leads per supplier at a rising price is the exact mechanism that produced the Q4 FY26–Q1 FY27 net-add declines in Silver, and there is no quantified retention/churn disclosure to prove Gold/Platinum is structurally immune to the same dynamic [`04_unit-economics.md`; `07_business-quality.md`; `12_red-flags-sweep.md`].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** management is actively working the demand side rather than treating it as background noise (re-testing Google as an acquisition channel, deliberately cutting "non-quality" buyer ad spend) [`12_red-flags-sweep.md`]; Platinum and Gold monthly churn remain under 1.5% through the same quarters that produced the Silver decline [`04_unit-economics.md`]; and the 5-year average return on capital (11.23%) still nominally clears the base-case estimated cost of capital (~8.75%), though that pass is not robust to a more conventional beta assumption [`09_moat.md`].

## 2. Specialist Roll-Up

| Specialist | Verdict Line | Biggest Finding |
|---|---|---|
| data-triage | Sufficient — audited FY26 Annual Report (~2.4 months old) plus Q1 FY27 quarterly filing and transcript (~3 weeks old), no extraction failures across 85 sources | Duplicate CIQ workbook exports are redundancy, not a coverage gap; no critical missing items |
| disqualifier-scan | No disqualifier triggered (0 of 8); 0 of 5 near-misses in band | An unnamed Designated Person's share-pledge pre-clearance lapse and a closed-window one-share trade are self-reported procedural lapses, not proven fraud — routed as a soft integrity note, not a lock |
| business-identity | India-focused, subscription-funded B2B marketplace; revenue = paying suppliers × ARPU | FY26 ARPU growth of 8% (11% for the top decile) is explicitly mix-driven (Silver → Gold/Platinum upgrades), not a base-price increase |
| segment-map | Web and related Services is the dominant — effectively sole economically material — segment: 91.96% of revenue, >100% of segment profit | Accounting Software Services (Busy Infotech/Livekeeping) was loss-making in 3 of the last 4 disclosed years, and goodwill impairment on those units is a named Key Audit Matter |
| unit-economics | Value creation is clear for the existing subscriber base (76% gross margin); unclear for the marginal new unit — no disclosed CAC or gross additions | Net paying-supplier additions turned negative in three of the last four quarters even as ARPU kept compounding at 8–9% |
| customer-geography | Geography-concentrated (99.6% India) business layered on a customer base with rising top-decile concentration | Gold+Platinum tier (~50% of paying suppliers) generates ~75% of revenue with no disclosed multi-year lock-in; top-decile-by-ARPU share rose from 41% (FY21) to 49% (FY26) |
| value-chain | Mixed economic control — near-total control on the input side, split control on the customer side by tier | A Silver-tier price increase in Q4 FY26 directly cost net supplier additions for two consecutive quarters; management stated "we are not going back on pricing" |
| business-quality | Aggregate 55/100 (Mixed/Average) | Customer stickiness and margin stability tie as the weakest factors (40 each) — no contractual lock-in, and a five-year segment EBITDA-margin range of 26.5%–40.9% (FY26 compressed 284bps) |
| competitive-map | Competitive position "Holding" (management-sourced proxy, no independent market-share data) | Paying-supplier growth decelerated sharply to +1.4% YoY in FY26 versus an 8% five-year CAGR, even though named rivals (TradeIndia, Just Dial) show no material gains against IndiaMART |
| moat | Narrow moat; trajectory stable with a specific near-term erosion warning | The economic-moat test (ROIC vs WACC) passes only on a low-beta (0.26) CAPM estimate (11.23% 5-yr ROIC vs ~8.75% WACC); under a more conventional small/mid-cap beta (~12.7–14.2% WACC) the same ROIC would sit at or below cost of capital |
| external-dependency | Partly externally driven; score 52/100 (inverted, higher = worse) | Management directly attributed roughly 1,000–1,500 of a ~1,200-supplier quarterly net loss in Q4 FY26 to a geopolitical shock ("the war"); India SME/MSME sentiment is named as the single biggest external lever |
| capital-allocation-governance | Capital allocation concerns; score 74/100; Filter-4 cap not triggered (acquisition-pattern severity 58 < 70) | A ~20-deal, decade-long pattern of mostly small minority venture stakes (self-funded, no debt) alongside one control acquisition (Busy Infotech); one subsidiary (Livekeeping) was struck off and one investment (Ten Times Online) divested at a nominal loss |
| red-flags-sweep | No new hard disqualifier; three new flags beyond upstream coverage | Management-confirmed buyer-side funnel stagnation on the Q1 FY27 call (severity 55) is the most material new flag, compounding with a newly incorporated lending subsidiary (severity 40) and founder key-person concentration with no disclosed succession plan (severity 35) |

## 3. Reconciliation

- **Paying-supplier count discrepancy.** `04_unit-economics.md` flags that the Q4 FY26 earnings-call transcript states a FY26 exit count of "228,000," which does not reconcile against that same call's own quarterly change figures or the Q1 FY27 call's base count — both independent transcript checks converge on ~219,800–219,850. Per the source hierarchy (audited filing beats transcript), this synthesis uses the FY26 Annual Report's audited figure of 220,000 and treats the transcript's 228,000 as an apparent transcription error, consistent with `04_unit-economics.md`'s own resolution.
- **Return on capital divergence.** `09_moat.md` flags a ~258bps gap between Capital IQ's vendor-reported FY26 Return on Capital (13.51%) and a hand-computed NOPAT-over-average-invested-capital figure (16.1%) built from the same underlying filing inputs. The gap could not be fully reconciled to a specific methodology difference. Per the conservative default (CLAUDE.md §4), this synthesis follows `09_moat.md` in using the lower, vendor-reported 13.51% FY26 / 11.23% five-year-average figures as the anchor for the moat and ROIC-versus-WACC read, not the higher hand-computed 16.1%.
- **Founder tenure and ownership — same facts, different framing.** `11_capital-allocation-governance.md` reads the co-founders' ~49% combined ownership and unbroken 27-year executive tenure (since 1999) as a high, stable alignment signal (severity 15/100, low). `12_red-flags-sweep.md` reads the identical facts as a key-person concentration risk, noting no succession plan, deputy-CEO designate, or continuity disclosure exists anywhere in the reviewed pool (severity 35/100). Both readings describe the same underlying fact accurately — high founder ownership and tenure is a genuine alignment positive, but the absence of any disclosed succession plan is a genuine, separate continuity risk. This synthesis carries both forward rather than netting them against each other: alignment is real, and so is the lack of a disclosed contingency plan for either founder's departure.
- No other material disagreements between specialists were found.

## 4. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- **Strongest business-model positive:** an asset-light, cash-generative subscription marketplace with no leverage — positive operating cash flow every year FY22–FY26 and LTM Jun-2026, ~₹31bn net cash, and standalone deferred revenue growing 14% in FY26, faster than the 9% growth in recognized revenue, a genuine forward demand signal [`01_disqualifier-scan.md`; `02_business-identity.md`].
- **Strongest business-model negative:** the core two-sided network is showing strain on both the buyer side (management-confirmed stagnation, Q1 FY27 call — severity 55, the most severe red flag in the pool) and the supplier side (a Silver-tier price rise turned net paying-supplier additions negative in three of the last four quarters) at the same time revenue keeps concentrating in the top decile of suppliers (41% → 49%, FY21–FY26) [`12_red-flags-sweep.md`; `04_unit-economics.md`; `05_customer-geography.md`]. This severity-55 flag must be read together with the severity-40 flag on the newly incorporated lending subsidiary, IndiaMART Finance Limited — a first move into credit-risk territory outside the core subscription model, initially framed by management as a partnership-lending structure rather than balance-sheet lending [`12_red-flags-sweep.md`].
- **Most important segment:** Web and related Services (the core marketplace) — 91.96% of FY26 consolidated revenue and more than 100% of segment profit; Accounting Software Services (Busy Infotech/Livekeeping) is a small, still-loss-making bolt-on with goodwill-impairment risk named as a Key Audit Matter [`03_segment-map.md`].
- **Cleanest unit-economics read:** the existing installed base of paying subscribers clearly creates value (76% gross margin, ~37% segment EBITDA-equivalent margin, ARPU compounding 8–9%/year for four straight years). The marginal new unit cannot be assessed — the company discloses net subscriber change only, not gross additions, churn by tier, or a customer acquisition cost, so a CAC-versus-lifetime-value comparison cannot be built [`04_unit-economics.md`].
- **Where the company sits vs named peers:** IndiaMART's LTM EBIT margin (32.0%) and gross margin (55.6%) both exceed the one disclosed same-country comparable, Just Dial (25.3% EBIT, 39.9% gross), though Just Dial's higher net margin is inflated by non-operating treasury income. No comparably-defined return-on-capital figure exists for Just Dial (only wide, unverified web-aggregator ROE/ROCE ranges), and the company's own most-cited "nearest" rival, TradeIndia, discloses no public financials at all [`08_competitive-map.md`; `09_moat.md`].
- **Main external dependency:** India SME/MSME sentiment and spending capacity — named by management as the direct cause of decelerating collection growth and negative net-subscriber quarters, compounded by a named geopolitical shock ("the war") that management directly blamed for 1,000–1,500 lost net supplier adds in a single quarter. This cannot be hedged the way FX or commodity risk can [`10_external-dependency.md`].
- **Most important capital allocation / governance signal:** a decade-long, ~20-deal pattern of mostly small minority venture-style investments (self-funded, no debt) alongside one control acquisition (Busy Infotech) — individually clean in structure (no leverage, no material related-party exposure) but a genuine opportunity-cost and management-attention drag, evidenced by one struck-off subsidiary (Livekeeping) and one investment divested at a nominal loss (Ten Times Online). This is the specific reason the Capital allocation & governance score sits at 74/100 rather than higher, even though it does not cross the ≥70-severity threshold that would trigger the Filter-4 cap [`11_capital-allocation-governance.md`].
- **Automatic disqualifier:** none triggered (0 of 8); 0 of 5 near-misses in band [`01_disqualifier-scan.md`].
- **Rejector filters tripped:** none of the three business-model-owned filters (crooks/integrity, serial acquirers, fast-changing industry) crossed its cap threshold. Filter 1 produced only a soft, sub-lock integrity note (routed to management-governance); Filter 4's acquisition-pattern severity (58) sits below the 70 cap threshold; Filter 5's industry rate-of-change score (45) sits above the 40 cap threshold. No score in this synthesis is capped by §24.
- **Biggest missing data point:** a quantified subscriber retention / net-revenue-retention / gross-churn-by-tier metric. Every downstream-relevant question — whether the recurring-revenue label is durable, whether Gold/Platinum is structurally immune to the pricing pushback already seen in Silver, and whether the marginal new subscriber creates value — traces back to this single absent disclosure [`02_business-identity.md`; `04_unit-economics.md`; `07_business-quality.md`].
- **Deeper work verdict:** the business deserves deeper work only if valuation already reflects the renewal-engine risk. The moat is narrow and its economic-moat test is not robust to a more conventional cost-of-capital assumption; business quality is mixed (55/100) with customer stickiness and margin stability as the two weakest factors; and the most severe red flag in the pool (buyer-side funnel stagnation) is a live, management-confirmed, current-quarter finding rather than a historical or hypothetical one. What would change the answer toward high-quality: a disclosed retention/NRR number showing Gold/Platinum durably insulated from the Silver-tier price dynamic, and two to three consecutive quarters of positive net paying-supplier additions alongside stable or improving segment EBITDA margin. What would change it toward low-quality: continued negative net additions spreading from Silver into Gold/Platinum, or a material write-down/scale-up of the newly incorporated lending subsidiary that turns a stated partnership-lending model into on-balance-sheet credit risk.

## 5. Simple Summary

- **What it does:** runs India's largest online business-to-business marketplace, connecting buyers who search for free with suppliers who pay to be found.
- **How it makes money:** subscription fees (Silver/Gold/Platinum tiers) from about 220,000 paying suppliers, collected upfront and recognized over the subscription period; a smaller accounting-software subsidiary (Busy Infotech) adds about 8% of revenue.
- **Whether each new unit creates value:** yes for the installed base (76% gross margin, ARPU compounding 8–9%/year); unclear for the next new subscriber, because the company does not disclose gross additions, tier-level churn, or acquisition cost.
- **Which segment matters most:** the core web marketplace — 92% of revenue and effectively all of segment profit; the accounting-software bolt-on has been loss-making in three of the last four years.
- **Whether it has a moat, and against whom:** a narrow moat built on distribution scale and network effects versus its closest rivals (TradeIndia, a smaller private company management has watched for years without material share shifts, and Just Dial, a comparable-scale rival recovering from a COVID-era decline) — not durable enough to clear a conventional cost-of-capital test with confidence.
- **What external variables it depends on:** India SME/MSME spending health and sentiment, plus a demonstrated sensitivity to geopolitical shocks that management has directly named as a cause of lost subscriber additions; commodity, FX, and debt-servicing risk are all negligible.
- **Whether capital is allocated well:** mostly — debt-free, cash-generative, well-covered dividends, and clean audit/related-party hygiene, offset by a decade of small, largely unproven minority venture bets that have produced at least one write-off and one loss-making exit.
- **Whether it deserves deeper work:** yes, but only if the price already discounts a renewal engine under simultaneous buyer-side stagnation and supplier-side price resistance — this is not, on the evidence gathered here, a durable compounder trading at a premium that evidence alone would justify.

## business-model / 02_business-identity.md

_Source: `business-model/02_business-identity.md`_

# Business Identity — INDIAMART

## 1. What The Company Actually Does

IndiaMART InterMESH Limited runs India's largest online B2B classifieds marketplace, where small and medium manufacturers, traders, and service providers ("suppliers") list their products so that business buyers can find and contact them [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, Business Overview, p.81]. As of March 31, 2026 the platform carried 129 million product listings across 98,000 categories and 57 industries, connecting 230 million registered buyers to 8.7 million registered suppliers [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, Business Overview, p.81]. Listing on the platform is free for most suppliers, but the company's revenue comes from the roughly 220,000 "paying suppliers" who buy an annual (or multi-year) subscription package — Silver, Gold, or Platinum — that gives them more visibility, priority placement, and access to a larger volume of buyer enquiries (called "RFQs" or "Buy-Leads") [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.82]. The problem the paying supplier is solving is customer acquisition: an MSME with no sales team or marketing budget pays IndiaMART for a steady stream of qualified buyer leads instead of building that reach itself. The business is almost entirely India-focused — the company states it "primarily serves the Indian market" and serves customers "in over 1,000 cities across India" through a nationwide sales and service network [Long Business Description, CIQ export; FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.82]. Alongside the core marketplace, the group also owns Busy Infotech (100%-owned), which sells subscription/license-based accounting and ERP software to MSMEs, plus minority equity stakes in a portfolio of adjacent MSME-tech startups (Vyapar, Livekeeping's parent, IDfy, Fleetx, Truckhall, Bizom, SuperProcure, EasyEcom, and others) [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, Board's Report — Subsidiaries & Associates, p.68-70].

## 2. How The Company Makes Money

Core marketplace (IndiaMART.com, standalone — ~90% of consolidated Revenue from Operations in FY26 [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83]):

`Revenue = Number of paying suppliers × Average annual subscription fee per supplier (ARPU)`

Standalone Revenue from Operations was ₹14,428.03 million in FY26 vs ₹13,200.58 million in FY25 (+9%) [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83]. Paying suppliers reached 220,000 (up from 217,000 in FY25, an 8-year CAGR of 8% since FY21's 152,000) and Average ARPU was approximately ₹66,000 per supplier for the year, up 8% year-on-year, with the top 10% of suppliers by ARPU growing 11% [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.82-83]. Suppliers on the higher Gold/Platinum tiers are about 50% of the paying-supplier base but contribute roughly 75% of operating revenue [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] — most of ARPU growth comes from suppliers trading up from the entry-level Silver tier rather than from price increases on Silver itself. Subscription fees are collected upfront regardless of the contract length and are then recognised as revenue evenly over the subscription period, with the unpaid-forward portion booked as Deferred Revenue (a contract liability) — standalone Deferred Revenue was ₹18,318 million at March 31, 2026, up 14% year-on-year [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83].

Accounting-software subsidiary (Busy Infotech, consolidated — the balance of the ~10 percentage-point gap between standalone and consolidated revenue: consolidated Revenue from Operations was ₹15,690.42 million in FY26 vs ₹13,883.44 million in FY25, +13% [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83]):

`Revenue = Number of licensed MSME customers × subscription/license fee per customer`

This is a much smaller, separately run software-subscription business and is not broken out to the ARPU/paying-supplier level of detail the core marketplace discloses in this filing.

What drives volume: net additions of paying suppliers (new sign-ups minus churn/downgrades to free). What drives price: the mix shift of existing suppliers moving from Silver into Gold/Platinum, plus category-based differential pricing on Platinum [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.82]. What drives margin: the cost of the roughly 5,376-person sales and customer-service organisation that acquires and services paying suppliers, plus technology/content spend — together employee benefits and outsourced sales costs were ~49% of standalone Revenue from Operations in FY26 [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83].

## 3. Business Type Classification

India-focused, subscription-funded B2B online marketplace (classifieds/lead-generation platform) for MSME suppliers, with a smaller consolidated accounting-software subscription subsidiary attached.

## 3a. Sector Overlay & Required-KPI Checklist

No row in `frameworks/SECTOR_OVERLAYS.md` names "online marketplace / classifieds" directly — IndiaMART is not a software vendor, bank, insurer, REIT, miner, oil & gas producer, retailer, telecom operator, asset manager, or pharma company. Its revenue mechanics, however, are functionally identical to the **SaaS / subscription software** row (tiered subscription packages, fees collected upfront and recognised over the contract term, Deferred Revenue as a contract liability, per-account ARPU) — and the consolidated group even includes a literal subscription-software subsidiary (Busy Infotech). This is a judgment call, not a literal-type match: I am applying the SaaS/subscription KPI grammar as the nearest analog because the data pool is organised around exactly those metrics, not because IndiaMART sells software.

| Required KPI (SaaS/subscription row) | Present / Absent in pool | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| cRPO / total RPO | Present (analog: Deferred Revenue) | Standalone Deferred Revenue ₹18,318 Mn (+14% YoY); consolidated ₹19,653 Mn (+17% YoY) [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] |
| Net retention (NRR) / gross retention or churn | **Absent — quantified figure not disclosed.** Only a qualitative statement that Gold/Platinum tiers show "materially higher retention rates" than Silver [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] | Data gap — flagged for downstream modules |
| Billings | Present (analog: Collection from Customers) | Standalone ₹16,743 Mn (+10% YoY); consolidated ₹18,567 Mn (+14% YoY) [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] |
| ARR & growth | Present (analog: Revenue from Operations) | Standalone ₹14,428 Mn (+9% YoY); consolidated ₹15,690 Mn (+13% YoY) [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] |
| Subscription vs services mix | Present | Standalone marketplace ≈90% of consolidated Revenue from Operations; Gold/Platinum tiers ≈75% of operating revenue from ≈50% of paying suppliers [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] |
| Stock-based comp as % of revenue | Present | Share-based payment expense ₹347.36 Mn in FY26 vs ₹168.87 Mn in FY25 (+106% YoY) against standalone revenue of ₹14,428 Mn ≈ 2.4% of revenue, roughly doubling as a share of a revenue base that grew only 9% [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, Note 21 (Employee Benefits Expense) / Note 28 (Share-Based Payment Plans)] |
| Rule-of-40 | Present (computable) | Standalone: revenue growth 9% + EBITDA margin 36% = 45 [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83]. Consolidated EBITDA margin was not located in the reviewed MD&A extract — noted as a partial gap for the consolidated cut |

Sector-specific red flags to watch (per the SaaS/subscription row, applied as the same analog): bookings decelerating while revenue holds — not currently observed, Deferred Revenue is growing faster than recognised revenue (+14% vs +9% standalone), which is a positive lead indicator, not a flag; SBC dilution masked by non-GAAP "profitability" — worth watching, since SBC expense roughly doubled year-on-year against high-single-digit revenue growth and standalone EBITDA margin already compressed 284bps; net retention slipping below ~100% — **not assessable, the underlying quantified retention/churn metric is absent from this pool** and should be requested directly (management commentary only gives a qualitative "Gold/Platinum retain better than Silver" claim, no number).

Valuation-norm analog: FCFF DCF on GAAP free cash flow (charging SBC), cross-checked against EV/NTM-revenue and a reverse-DCF read of what growth the market is pricing in — consistent with the SaaS/subscription row.

## 4. What Drives Variance

Revenue moves mainly on net paying-supplier additions (volume) and on the pace at which existing suppliers upgrade from Silver into Gold/Platinum (mix/price) — FY26's ARPU growth of 8% (11% for the top decile) was explicitly a mix effect, not a base-price increase [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.82-83]. Margin moves mainly on the cost of the supplier-facing sales and service organisation (employee benefits plus outsourced sales cost, ~49% of standalone revenue in FY26) and on technology/content spend, both of which rose faster than revenue in FY26, compressing standalone EBITDA margin by 284bps to 36% [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83]. Because the marketplace collects subscription cash upfront and recognises it over the contract term, reported revenue growth (9% standalone) lags cash collections growth (10% standalone) and the change in Deferred Revenue (+14% standalone) — the deferred-revenue balance is the better near-term read on underlying demand than the income-statement revenue line in any single period. At the consolidated level, standalone net profit (₹5,252 Mn) exceeded consolidated net profit (₹4,747 Mn) in FY26, meaning the minority stakes in the Busy Infotech subsidiary and the associate-company portfolio (Vyapar, and others carried under the equity method) were a net drag on consolidated earnings that period [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, p.83] — a source of variance separate from the core marketplace's own operating performance.

| Web and related Services | Online B2B marketplace connecting buyers and suppliers of business products/services in India; "provides a platform to discover products and services and connect with the suppliers of such products and services" [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32] | 91.96% (₹14,429.38m) | 100.5% (₹5,328.56m of ₹5,300.41m total) | High — segment EBITDA margin ~36.9% in FY26 (₹5,328.56m / ₹14,429.38m), and has stayed double-digit every year FY22–FY26 (27.4%–40.9%) [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32; Financials (1).xls, Segments tab] | Low — asset-light platform; company discloses no material segment capex after FY22 (last disclosed standalone-era capex, FY21, was ₹0.3m) [Financials (1).xls, Segments tab]. Balance-sheet "Segment assets" of ₹31,409.91m are not disaggregated into fixed vs financial assets in the segment note, so this is a qualitative read, not a capex-ratio calculation | Mid — revenue sits on a subscription/prepaid-billing model, cushioned near-term by ₹12,202m of contract liabilities (deferred, already-collected billings) on the FY26 balance sheet [FY26 Annual Report, Balance Sheet], but renewals depend on discretionary MSME marketing spend that tracks the broader Indian SME economy — Inference, not from filings | Subscriber renewal/collection risk in a discretionary-spend category, and competitive pressure from alternative lead-generation channels — Inference, not from filings (this segment's own competitive dynamics are outside this agent's scope; see `competitive-map`) |
| Accounting Software Services | Development, system analysis, design and marketing of integrated business accounting software for MSMEs, run through two wholly-owned subsidiaries: Busy Infotech Private Limited (formerly Tolexo Online, 100% owned, acquired for ~INR 500 crore per management) and Livekeeping Technologies Private Limited (100% owned) [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32; Note on related entities p.1213/1215; Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21 2026 prepared remarks] | 8.04% (₹1,261.04m) | (0.5)% (₹(28.15)m of ₹5,300.41m total — a segment loss) | Low — segment result was negative in 3 of the last 4 disclosed years: FY24 −7.2% margin, FY25 −17.5%, FY26 −2.2% (narrowing loss); only FY23 was positive at +23.5% [Financials (1).xls, Segments tab; FY26 Annual Report, Note 32] | Low/Mid — software-product business, but goodwill of ₹4,122.34m (Busy Infotech) and ₹420.38m (Livekeeping Technologies) sits on the balance sheet from the acquisitions, and the FY26 auditor flagged goodwill impairment as a Key Audit Matter requiring judgement on revenue-growth, terminal-growth and WACC assumptions [FY26 Annual Report, Independent Auditor's Report, "Goodwill Impairment," Note 6A] | Mid — early-stage SaaS-style billing growth (Busy Infotech billed ~INR 59 crore in Q1 FY27, up from ~INR 10 crore a year earlier per management commentary) [Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21 2026], less exposed to broad MSME ad-spend cycles than the core marketplace but sensitive to continued investment/scaling decisions — Inference, not from filings | Persistent segment-level losses and goodwill-impairment risk on the Busy Infotech / Livekeeping cash-generating units, explicitly named a Key Audit Matter by the statutory auditor (B S R & Co. LLP) [FY26 Annual Report, Independent Auditor's Report, "Goodwill Impairment"] |

Note on a related, non-consolidated entity: Simply Vyapar Apps Private Limited (~28.6%–28.7% stake) is accounted for as an **associate** (equity method), not a subsidiary, and its revenue/profit is NOT included in either segment above — it shows up only as "Share in net loss of associates" (−₹547.72m in FY26) below the segment-result line [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32; shareholding note p.1224]. Do not conflate Vyapar with the "Accounting Software Services" segment, which is Busy Infotech + Livekeeping.

## 2. Dominant Segment

Web and related Services is the dominant — and effectively the only economically material — segment. It generated 91.96% of FY26 consolidated revenue (₹14,429.38m of ₹15,690.42m) and more than 100% of FY26 segment profit, because the Accounting Software Services segment posted a small operating loss (segment result of ₹(28.15)m) that year [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32]. On both the revenue test and the profit test, Web and related Services clears the 85% single-segment threshold: this is best read as a single-segment business with a small, currently loss-making, fast-growing bolt-on (Accounting Software Services), not a genuinely multi-segment company. At the standalone (parent-only) level the company does not disclose segment information at all — "the Company has disclosed the segment information only as part of consolidated financial statements" [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32, Standalone Financial Statements] — underscoring that the marketplace business is effectively the whole of the standalone entity.

## 3. Segment Disclosure Quality

Segment definitions have been consistent for the trailing three fiscal years (FY24, FY25, FY26 all report the same two segments, "Web and related Services" and "Accounting Software Services," with identical wording of the segment description note) [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32; Q1 FY27 Interim Report, Note 29]. The structure did change further back: FY21 was reported as a single combined segment ("Business-To-Business E-Marketplace"), and the Accounting Software Services segment first appears in FY23 following the Busy Infotech acquisition [Financials (1).xls, Segments tab] — this predates the trailing-three-year window and is noted for completeness, not as a current disclosure gap. There is no "Other" or residual revenue bucket — 100% of consolidated revenue is allocated between the two named segments in every disclosed year. The one unallocated item is on the balance sheet, not revenue: an "Unallocable" assets line of ₹7,629.29m in FY26, 16.5% of total segment assets of ₹46,246.03m [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32] — likely unattributed cash/investments, but the filing does not itemise it, so this is flagged as a minor gap. Profit is disclosed at segment level down to "Segment results" (operating profit before finance cost, D&A, other income, associate losses and tax), but the company does NOT split net profit after tax, finance cost, other income, or the associate-loss line (which is material — ₹(547.72)m in FY26, almost entirely attributable to the Vyapar associate) by segment; only consolidated totals are given below the segment-result line [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32]. Segment-level capital expenditure has not been disclosed since FY21 (only Assets and Liabilities are broken out for FY22 onward) [Financials (1).xls, Segments tab], which limits how precisely capital intensity can be judged per segment (see Section 1 note above). Downstream agents (`unit-economics`, `competitive-map`, `business-quality`) should treat the segment-level margin and capex reads as directional, not precise, given these gaps.

## business-model / 04_unit-economics.md

_Source: `business-model/04_unit-economics.md`_

# Unit Economics — INDIAMART

## 1. Natural Unit

The natural economic unit for Web and related Services (the dominant segment — 91.96% of FY26 consolidated revenue and effectively all of segment profit per `03_segment-map.md`) is **the paying subscriber**: a supplier on the IndiaMART marketplace who pays for a Silver, Gold, or Platinum subscription package, in exchange for listing, lead volume (Request-for-Quote access), and buyer-discovery tools [FY26 Annual Report, p.81–82].

The small, loss-making Accounting Software Services segment (8.04% of revenue, run through Busy Infotech and Livekeeping) has a different natural unit — the software licence / billing account (management cites "new licences sold," e.g. ~54,000 cumulative as of Q1 FY27) — but it is not built out below because it is not the dominant segment and its per-unit economics are not separately disclosed [Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21 2026, prepared remarks].

## 2. Unit Economics Table

All figures are for the Web and related Services (marketplace) segment / IndiaMART standalone entity, FY26 (year ended 31 March 2026) unless stated. "Paying subscriber" count used for per-unit division is the company's own year-end disclosed figure: 220,000 at 31 March 2026, up from 217,000 at 31 March 2025 [FY26 Annual Report, p.81, p.83]. Note: the Q4 FY26 earnings-call transcript (Apr 30, 2026) states the FY26 exit count as "2,28,000" (228,000) — this does not reconcile with the same call's own disclosed Q4 decline of 1,200 from a Q3 FY26 exit count of 221,000 [Q3 FY26 earnings call, Jan 20 2026] (221,000 − 1,200 = 219,800), nor with the Q1 FY27 call's statement that the base was 218,000 after a 1,850 net decline in the quarter (218,000 + 1,850 = 219,850) [Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21 2026]. Both independent checks converge on ~219,800–219,850, matching the Annual Report's 220,000. Per the source hierarchy (audited filing beats transcript), this report uses the Annual Report's 220,000 and flags the transcript's 228,000 as an apparent transcription error rather than silently using it.

| Unit Economic | Value | Period | Direction vs Prior Year | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue per unit (Average Revenue Per User / ARPU — revenue from operations ÷ paying suppliers at year-end) | ₹66,000 per paying subscriber | FY26 | **Improving** — up from ₹61,000 in FY25 (+8.2%); company states "overall ARPU grew by 8%" | [FY26 Annual Report, p.82–83, "Average ARPU" chart and footnote: "ARPU represents Revenue from Operations for the respective Financial Year divided by Paying Subscription Suppliers at the respective year-end"] |
| Gross margin per unit (standalone Gross Margin = Revenue from Operations − Customer Service Cost) | 76% margin ≈ ₹50,160 gross profit per subscriber (₹66,000 ARPU × 76%, derived — Inference, not from filings) | FY26 | **Mixed** — margin % ticked down slightly, from 77% (FY25) to 76% (FY26), −82 basis points (bps — hundredths of a percentage point), but the derived rupee amount per subscriber rose (~₹50,160 FY26 vs ~₹46,970 FY25, +6.8%) because ARPU grew faster than the margin fell | [FY26 Annual Report, p.82, "Financial Overview – Standalone" table: Gross Profit ₹10,995m / ₹14,428m revenue = 76% FY26; ₹10,168m / ₹13,201m = 77% FY25] |
| Contribution margin per unit (after variable costs) | Not disclosed as a distinct line. Nearest proxies: standalone EBITDA margin 36% FY26 (down from 39% FY25, −284 bps); Web-segment EBITDA-equivalent ("Segment results") margin 36.9% FY26 (₹5,328.56m / ₹14,429.38m) vs 40.5% FY25 (₹5,347.08m / ₹13,201.53m), a fall of ~360 bps | FY26 | **Deteriorating** on the margin-% basis; on a per-subscriber rupee basis, segment EBITDA-equivalent per subscriber was ~₹24,220 (FY26: ₹5,328.56m ÷ 220,000) vs ~₹24,641 (FY25: ₹5,347.08m ÷ 217,000) — down ~1.7% (derived, Inference, not from filings) | [FY26 Annual Report, p.82 standalone EBITDA table; Note 32 Segment Information — Segment results by segment, FY26 and FY25] |
| Cost to acquire / build the unit (Customer Acquisition Cost) | Not disclosed. The company reports Selling & Marketing expense (₹2,290m FY26, 16% of revenue, up from ₹1,806m / 14% in FY25, +27% YoY) and Customer Service Cost (₹3,433m FY26, up 13%), but does not split spend between acquiring new subscribers versus servicing/upselling the existing base, and does not disclose gross subscriber additions (only net change) — so a true CAC cannot be computed from disclosure | FY26 | **Unknown** (input not disclosed at the granularity needed) | [FY26 Annual Report, p.82, "Financial Overview – Standalone" table (Selling & Marketing, Customer Service Cost lines); "Our major expenses primarily comprise employee benefits and outsourced sales costs, which together accounted for 49% of revenue from operations in FY 2025-26," p.81] |
| Payback period or unit lifetime | Not disclosed as a formal payback metric or cohort survival curve. Management-disclosed churn by tier (a proxy for unit lifetime): Platinum "much less than 1%" per month; Gold ~1%–1.5% per month; combined paid tiers ~1% per month overall; Silver ~7% per month (monthly-billing cohort) / ~4% (annual-billing cohort) | Q4 FY26 (as of Apr 30, 2026) and reconfirmed Q1 FY27 (Jul 21, 2026) | **Stable** — management states repeatedly, across at least two consecutive quarters, that these churn rates are essentially unchanged ("nothing has changed" on Silver monthly churn); most of the churn is concentrated in the first 12 months after onboarding, with retention improving markedly from year two onward | [Q4 FY26 earnings call, Apr 30 2026, prepared remarks and Q&A: "monthly churn rates in the Platinum segment being much less than 1% and in the Gold segment anywhere 1% to 1.5%... on overall basis, about approximately 1% per month. While on the Silver, annual, they are about 4% and the Silver monthly, they are about 7%"; Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21 2026, Q&A: "From that 7% silver monthly, I think nothing has changed... the first 12 months is the biggest issue... we see the renewal and retention rate improve double back from the second year onwards"] |

Gold and Platinum subscribers — roughly 50% of the paying-subscriber base — generate more than 75% of revenue and are described by management as having "good upsell and retention rate," while Silver is the entry tier carrying most of the churn [FY26 Annual Report, p.81; Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21 2026]. This is a materially bimodal unit, not a single homogenous one — the table above reflects the blended average.

## 3. Value Creation Read

**Unclear for the marginal new unit; the average installed unit clearly creates value.** The *existing* paying-subscriber base is high-margin — 76% gross margin and a ~37% segment EBITDA-equivalent margin in FY26 [FY26 Annual Report, p.82; Note 32] — and revenue per unit (ARPU) has grown every year for at least four years (₹46,000 → ₹66,000, FY23–FY26, an 8–9% compound rate) [FY26 Annual Report, p.83]. That supports a "creates value" read for the stock of subscribers already on the books, cushioned further by ₹18,318m of standalone deferred revenue (cash already collected for service not yet delivered) [FY26 Annual Report, p.82]. But the question this section must answer is about the *next* unit, and that math cannot be completed from disclosure: the company does not publish gross subscriber additions (only net change), a customer acquisition cost, or a cohort-level lifetime-value figure, so contribution margin × unit lifetime cannot be compared to acquisition cost as required to prove marginal-unit value creation. What the disclosed data does show is a warning sign, not a conclusion: Selling & Marketing cost per subscriber rose ~25% YoY (from ~₹8,323 to ~₹10,409, derived from the FY26/FY25 S&M spend and subscriber counts — Inference, not from filings) while net subscriber growth stalled and went negative in three of the last four disclosed quarters (Q3 FY26: −1,000; Q4 FY26: −1,200; Q1 FY27: −1,850) [Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27 earnings calls]. Segment EBITDA-equivalent margin also fell ~360 bps FY25→FY26. The single most valuable missing disclosure is gross subscriber additions and gross churn broken out by tier (Silver/Gold/Platinum), which would let a CAC-versus-lifetime-value comparison actually be built; without it, the marginal-unit read stays **Unclear**.

## 4. Sensitivity

Silver-tier churn and gross additions are the input most likely to move the value-creation read if they shift 20%, and the evidence shows this has historically been the most volatile line, not the most stable one. Silver monthly churn (~7%) has stayed roughly flat per management commentary, but *gross additions* have swung enough on their own to flip net subscriber change from positive (+2,800 net in Q2 FY26, before a one-time onboarding benefit) to negative in the next three quarters running, following an August–September 2025 price increase on the Silver tier [Q2 FY26, Q3 FY26, Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27 earnings calls]. A 20% further deterioration in Silver gross additions or churn would likely keep net subscriber growth negative for another year and would compress the denominator in every per-unit metric above (ARPU, segment EBITDA per subscriber) even if ARPU itself keeps rising, because a shrinking, more Gold/Platinum-skewed base changes the mix the average is drawn from. By contrast, ARPU (price per unit) has been comparatively stable and management-controlled, compounding at 8–9% for four straight years even through the same churn episode [FY26 Annual Report, p.83] — a 20% move in ARPU would be a larger and more unusual swing than anything seen in the last four years, whereas a 20% move in Silver churn/gross-additions is within the range the company has already lived through in FY26 alone.

# Customer And Geography Map — INDIAMART

## 1. Customer Map

IndiaMART does not name individual customers in its filings (its own segment note confirms no single customer clears the disclosure threshold). What it does disclose is a **tiered concentration**: revenue is split across roughly 220,000 paying suppliers (sellers), but a shrinking slice of that base drives most of the revenue. Buyers pay nothing — IndiaMART's paying "customer" is always the supplier/seller side of its marketplace.

| Customer Type | Importance (% of revenue if disclosed) | Long-term Contract? (Y/N/Not disclosed) | Evidence | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Named single customer (any) | No single customer represents 10% or more of total revenue, for the Company or the Group, in FY24, FY25 or FY26 | Not disclosed | FY26 Annual Report (Ind AS), Notes to Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements, segment note ("No single customer represents 10% or more of the Group's total revenue for the year ended 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2025") | Low — no bilateral counterparty risk from one name |
| Gold + Platinum tier paying suppliers (~110K accounts, ~50% of the 220K paying-supplier base) | "Nearly 75% of our operating revenues" (FY26 Integrated Annual Report); management separately described this cohort on calls as "more than 75% of revenue" | N — subscription packages, renewed annually/monthly; no multi-year lock-in disclosed | FY26 Integrated Annual Report, p.82 ("Suppliers in the Gold and Platinum tiers account for approximately 50% of our paying supplier base and contribute nearly 75% of our operating revenues"); Q4 FY26 earnings call, Apr 30, 2026, prepared remarks ("Platinum and Gold customers, which constitute approximately 50% of our customer base and more than 75% of revenue"); Q1 FY27 earnings call, Jul 21, 2026, prepared remarks (same ~50%/>75% language) | High — three-quarters of revenue sits in a subscription cohort that self-selects into and out of the top two of three pricing tiers |
| Top 10% of paying suppliers, by ARPU | 49% of revenue from operations in FY26, up from 41% in FY21 (41% → 44% → 46% → 46% → 47% → 49%, FY21–FY26) | N — subscription, not contract | FY26 Integrated Annual Report, p.83, "ARPU of Top 10% Customers" chart | High and rising — concentration in the top decile has widened every year disclosed |
| Top 1% of paying suppliers, by ARPU | 16% of revenue from operations in FY26 (14% → 16% → 17% → 16% → 16% → 16%, FY21–FY26) | N | FY26 Integrated Annual Report, p.83, "ARPU of Top 1% Customers" chart | Medium — roughly one-sixth of revenue sits with ~2,200 accounts (1% of 220K paying suppliers) |
| Silver-tier (entry-level) paying suppliers (~110K accounts, remaining ~50% of the paying-supplier base) | Residual ~25% of revenue (100% − ~75% Gold/Platinum share); Q4 FY26 net-add deceleration was attributed to this cohort | N | Q4 FY26 earnings call, Apr 30, 2026, prepared remarks: "total number of paying suppliers increased by 3,200 to 2,28,000, while the quarter 4 saw a little decline of 1,200. This decrease can primarily be attributed to moderation in gross addition, due to price increase we implemented in the silver subscription tier" | Medium — this cohort is the most price-sensitive and the entry funnel for future Gold/Platinum upgrades; a Silver price rise already dented gross additions in Q4 FY26 |
