- Biggest earnings driver (one line): Paying-subscriber net additions to the Web segment — ARPU has done all of the realized revenue growth for two straight years, but the subscriber base it multiplies has been flat to shrinking (net adds negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters), and management has declined to give a timeline for when that turns.
- Biggest earnings risk (one line): The current "elevated" 35.35% EBITDA margin (a temporary, management-labelled policy choice to defer customer-acquisition spend) and the falling paying-subscriber count may be the same underlying SME-demand weakness expressed twice rather than two independent, offsetting forces — if so, margin and revenue miss together instead of offsetting.
- **Red-flag Severity Verdict (from 08_earnings-red-flags, reported verbatim): Material concerns** — high-severity flags present; earnings setup may be overstated or fragile.

## 1A. Module Disconfirmation

- **Strongest bear point:** Revenue growth has decelerated every year since FY23 (30.78%→21.45%→16.01%→13.02%→11.37% in Q1 FY27, the softest of the last 8 quarters), and the volume half of the revenue engine — paying-subscriber net adds — has been negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters with no management timeline for a turn [02_revenue-drivers §4, §7].
- **Strongest bull point (steelman):** ARPU has compounded ~8–9% for four straight years with no reversal in the data, and cash conversion is structurally excellent — CFO has exceeded EBITDA in every one of the last 5 years (121%–182%), funded by deferred revenue that has never declined in the company's history [01_historical-financials §1; 06_earnings-quality §2–3].
- **Single killer risk specific to this module:** The compounding scenario where the margin tailwind (deferred acquisition spend) and the revenue drag (falling net adds) are not independent policy/demand levers but the same SME-demand weakness expressed twice — if the churn-resolution timeline management gave ("2, 3 more quarters") slips, margin and revenue would miss together, not offset [05_beat-miss-setup §10; 07_earnings-sensitivity §5; 08_earnings-red-flags §2.6, flagged Critical].
- **Disconfirming evidence already visible:** The CEO admitted directly on the Q1 FY27 call that "the overall number of buyers are stagnating" in the same quarter management is deliberately holding back acquisition spend — a leading indicator corroborating the shared-root-cause read rather than two independent forces [business-model `12_red-flags-sweep` §2, cited via 08_earnings-red-flags §2.6].

## 3. Reconciliation

The specialist agents (00–07) themselves report no material factual disagreements — 08_earnings-red-flags confirms this explicitly, noting the only conflicting figures found are internal to the Capital IQ vendor exports (an ~2.2% EBITDA reconciliation gap across CIQ's own tabs, and two different FQ4 FY26 EPS-Normalized figures within the same workbook family), both already transparently flagged by the agents that touched them rather than silently resolved, and neither material enough to change a qualitative trend read.

There is, however, a genuine difference in **interpretive stance** between 05_beat-miss-setup's "balanced" verdict (and, relatedly, 04_guidance-consensus's "fair" bar) on one side, and 08_earnings-red-flags' argument that this framing understates fragility on the other. 05 constructed the "balanced" call by treating the margin tailwind (deferred acquisition spend) and the revenue drag (falling subscriber net adds) as two roughly offsetting forces — and 05's own Section 10 pre-mortem independently names the risk that these are not offsetting but causally linked. 08 escalates this same risk to Critical severity, cross-corroborating it with 07_earnings-sensitivity's interaction-effects section (§5) and the business-model module's finding that the CEO admitted buyer-side stagnation on the same call the spend pullback is occurring. Per CLAUDE.md §4 (use the more conservative interpretation when sources point in different directions), this synthesis adopts the more cautious reading: the verdict here is **Mixed earnings setup** rather than 05's face-value "balanced" framing or a clean "stable" call — surfacing both views rather than silently picking one, consistent with 08's own recommendation in its Section 6 that "the verdict should lean toward 'Mixed earnings setup' rather than a clean 'stable/balanced' read, pending the next 1–2 quarters of evidence."

## 5. Earnings Setup Summary

### Revenue Setup

The current growth rate is sustainable in the sense that it rests on a recurring, structural lever — four straight years of ~8–9% ARPU growth on a subscription base — rather than M&A, FX, or an accounting change; there is no reported-vs-organic gap to name here because no acquisition or divestiture touches either compared period. But sustainability now depends entirely on one factor: whether paying-subscriber net additions turn positive again, because ARPU growth applied to a shrinking or flat subscriber base compounds against a smaller pool every quarter, and management itself has warned that pushing price further while renewal is weak risks making customer-acquisition cost rise faster than lifetime value. The single factor that would flip the direction of revenue growth is that subscriber net adds — negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters — either turn positive (confirming the current setup is a temporary soft patch) or stay negative through the "2, 3 quarter" window management itself flagged (confirming a genuine, not cyclical, demand problem). One further nuance worth flagging: the fast-growing Accounting Software Services segment, only 8% of FY26 revenue, supplied roughly a third (3.48 of 11.37 percentage points) of Q1 FY27's incremental growth — a segment mix shift that is real and disclosed, not a residual gap, but one riding on a much smaller, still loss-making base than the core marketplace.

### Margin Setup

Current margins are not sustainable through the next few quarters as reported — Q1 FY27's 35.35% EBITDA margin is a management-labelled temporary policy choice (deferred customer-acquisition spend), not a cyclical peak or trough in the traditional sense, and management has stated it plans to hold this stance for roughly "2, 3 more quarters" before resuming spend. The single driver that, moving adversely by 10–20%, takes the largest bite out of consolidated margins is discretionary customer-acquisition opex (Advertisement + Outsourced sales): resuming Advertisement spend to management's own guided ~₹10 crore/quarter run-rate would cost roughly a quarter of FY26 EBITDA on its own (up to −24.2% per 07_earnings-sensitivity's bear case). IndiaMART has no contractual or structural margin-protection mechanism in the traditional sense — there is no COGS line, no commodity pass-through, and no hedging, because the business has no input-cost exposure at all; the only lever management holds is its own discretion over acquisition spend, which is precisely the lever currently propping the margin up and the lever most likely to reverse it.

### Quality Check

The single largest gap between reported and economic earnings is the ~30% of FY26 Profit Before Tax and ~40% of diluted EPS that comes from mark-to-market and realised gains on the company's ~₹30 billion treasury book — a gap that is not narrowing; it has recurred at material size in every one of the last 5 fiscal years despite Capital IQ's own income-statement structure labelling it "Unusual Items." This is not an aggressive adjustment management is using to flatter results — it is fully disclosed under Ind AS fair-value accounting, is real, collected value, and IndiaMART does not publish any non-GAAP overlay of its own to compare it against. To model normalized earnings for next year, the correct starting point is GAAP EBIT/EBITDA, not GAAP PBT or diluted EPS, because EBIT/EBITDA already sit above the treasury-gains line in IndiaMART's own P&L structure and exclude this volatile, market-linked item entirely — while PBT and EPS embed it and have therefore swung far more than the operating business has (diluted EPS fell −72% quarter over quarter in one instance on an EBITDA base that moved only −1.2%).

### Consensus Bar

For IndiaMART to beat the current bar by a material margin, two things would need to happen roughly at once — paying-subscriber net adds turning positive meaningfully ahead of management's own "2, 3 quarter" timeline, and EBITDA margin holding near Q1 FY27's elevated level rather than reverting — which is the same conjunction risk 08_earnings-red-flags flags as the module's single biggest vulnerability, not two independent paths to a beat. The bar looks most likely mis-set on the EPS line specifically: consensus FY2027 EPS growth (+16.8%) outpaces consensus FY2027 EBITDA growth (+11.96%) by 4.8 percentage points, a gap that — given FY26's demonstrated EPS dependency on the volatile treasury-gains line (~30–40% of PBT/EPS) — plausibly embeds an unstated assumption that this non-operating item recurs or grows; if it does not, an EPS "miss" could occur even alongside healthy operating performance. The revenue bar, by contrast, looks correctly priced: it has been tightly calibrated to actual results (0% to +1.3% surprise) for four straight quarters, including an exactly in-line Q1 FY27 print, so a large surprise in either direction on the top line next quarter would be the exception, not the pattern.

## 5b. Leverage & Capital Structure

Leverage is within normal range and did not change materially during the period — no dedicated treatment required. IndiaMART carries no bank borrowings; its entire "Total Debt" per Capital IQ is lease liabilities (₹231.02mn at FY26-end), and the company has held a structural net-cash position on both the strict basis (total debt minus cash) and the broad basis (also netting short-term investments and the treasury book) throughout the full 5-year window reviewed, deepening from ₹122mn net cash (strict, FY23) to ₹573mn (strict, FY26) and exceeding ₹30 billion net cash on the broad basis in FY26 [01_historical-financials §1]. Neither Trigger A (net debt/Adjusted EBITDA > 3.0x) nor Trigger B (a material YoY leverage increase) fires.

## 6. Key Numbers

- Revenue growth rate: +13.02% FY26 YoY; +11.37% Q1 FY27 YoY, the softest of the last 8 quarters [01_historical-financials §1, §3]
- EBITDA margin: 33.18% FY26 (CIQ-sourced) / 33.78% (company's own audited ratio); Q1 FY27 35.35%, management-labelled "elevated" and temporary [01_historical-financials §1; 03_margin-drivers §3, §8]
- EPS (diluted): ₹78.77 FY26 (−14.0% YoY); Q1 FY27 ₹28.56, largely driven by a ₹107cr treasury mark-to-market gain, not core operations [01_historical-financials §1; 05_beat-miss-setup §6]
- CFO / EBITDA: 133.4% FY26; range 121%–182% across all of the last 5 years, never once approaching the 70% "healthy" line [06_earnings-quality §1–2]
- Biggest driver current level: ARPU ₹66,000/paying-subscriber, FY26, +8.2% YoY; paying-subscriber count 218,000, flat YoY, net decline of 1,850 within Q1 FY27 alone [02_revenue-drivers §4]
- Consensus gap (if available): FY2027E EPS growth (+16.8%) outpaces FY2027E EBITDA growth (+11.96%) by ~4.8pp — a gap 08_earnings-red-flags attributes to an implicit assumption about non-operating treasury gains recurring [04_guidance-consensus §3; 08_earnings-red-flags §2.5]
- Estimate revision direction: Revenue and EPS revision breadth net negative (−28.6% and −14.3% of 14 analysts, last 3 months) while EBITDA breadth is net positive (+28.6%); target price revisions sharply negative (1 up/16 down of 18 analysts); average recommendation drifted Outperform→Hold over 6–12 months [04_guidance-consensus §5]
- Earnings volatility score: 66/100 (inverted, higher = worse), High-volatility band; discretionary acquisition opex and the treasury-book NAV are the two largest single swing variables [07_earnings-sensitivity §7]

## 7. What Would Change The Earnings Verdict?

| Current Verdict | What Would Upgrade It | What Would Downgrade It | Data Needed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mixed earnings setup | Paying-subscriber net adds turn positive for 2+ consecutive quarters WHILE EBITDA margin holds near or above the Q1 FY27 34–35% level as acquisition spend resumes on schedule — proving the margin tailwind and the demand drag are genuinely independent policy/demand levers, not the same weakness (would support "Earnings stable" or "Earnings inflecting — positive, subscriber recovery") | Net adds stay negative through Q3–Q4 FY27 (past management's own "2, 3 quarter" window), and/or customer-acquisition spend resumes toward the guided ~₹10 crore/quarter run-rate before subscriber trends recover — confirming the Critical compounding scenario and pulling both revenue and margin down together (would support "Earnings decelerating") | Next 1–2 quarters of paying-subscriber net-add data and confirmation of whether acquisition spend actually resumes on the stated timeline; segment-level Street consensus for the Accounting Software Services (Busy) segment to cross-check its guided 27–30% CAGR; explicit disclosure or confirmation of whether FY2027 consensus EPS assumes the treasury mark-to-market gains line recurs at a similar size to FY26 |

Consensus setup here is not "Unknown" — it is present, current, and scored at 48/100 — so the constraint against calling "Earnings accelerating" with unknown consensus does not directly apply. Even so, nothing in the evidence (decelerating revenue, negative subscriber volume, a temporary margin prop, and de-rating sell-side sentiment) supports an accelerating call; the offsetting-but-fragile pattern across drivers is what places this at Mixed rather than Stable, Decelerating, or Accelerating.

## 8. Note To The Final Synthesizer

- Dominant earnings trend: revenue growth has decelerated every year since FY23 and is now driven almost entirely by price (ARPU), not volume — the subscriber base the price is applied against is flat to shrinking.
- **Critical red flag (must not be dropped):** the "balanced" beat/miss setup (margin tailwind from deferred spend vs. revenue drag from falling net adds) may actually be one underlying SME-demand weakness expressed through two channels — if the two forces are not independent, they miss together rather than offsetting [08_earnings-red-flags §2.6, Critical].
- **High-severity flag:** ~30% of FY26 Profit Before Tax and ~40% of diluted EPS come from a recurring (5 straight years), non-operating treasury mark-to-market gain that vendor labelling misclassifies as "unusual" — headline EPS/PBT are a noisier earnings-quality signal than EBIT/EBITDA for this company [08_earnings-red-flags §2.7].
- **High-severity flag:** consensus FY2027 EPS growth outpaces consensus EBITDA growth by ~4.8pp, an inconsistency that likely embeds an unstated assumption that the volatile treasury-gains line recurs or grows — an EPS "miss" could occur even with healthy operating performance [08_earnings-red-flags §2.5].
- **High-severity flag:** the current 35.35% EBITDA margin is a temporary, management-labelled policy choice (deferred acquisition spend), with a reversal risk management itself named within "2, 3" quarters — any read that treats this level as the new baseline is likely overstated [08_earnings-red-flags §2.4].
- **High-severity flag:** realized revenue growth is now entirely price/ARPU-driven; paying-subscriber volume has been flat-to-negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters with no management timeline for a turn [08_earnings-red-flags §2.3].
- **Red-flag Severity Verdict (verbatim from 08): Material concerns.**
- Whether earnings are clean and cash-backed: yes on cash — CFO has exceeded EBITDA every year for 5 years and deferred revenue has never declined — but headline EPS/PBT carry a large, recurring, market-linked non-operating component that should not be read as an operating signal.
- Consensus bar assessment: rated "fair," not clearly low or high; the EPS bar for FY2027 specifically looks set too high relative to what operating (EBITDA) growth alone would support.
- Next-quarter setup and second-quarter look-ahead: rated "balanced" by the beat/miss specialist, but this synthesis treats that framing with more caution given the compounding-scenario risk; visibility into Q3 FY27 (the quarter after next) is limited, and management's own "2, 3 quarter" timeline for churn resolution would place the true test around Q3–Q4 FY27, not the upcoming print.
- Top sensitivity variable and its current direction: the largest single number in the sensitivity table is the treasury-book NAV (±5% move → ±₹1,426mn PBT, an external, symmetric market-risk exposure); the largest lever on operating earnings specifically is discretionary customer-acquisition opex, currently a tailwind that management has signalled it will unwind.
- Whether any partial-data cap applied and what it limits: none — data sufficiency triage returned "Sufficient" with zero active caps (Section 4).
- Biggest missing data point: whether acquisition spend actually resumes on management's stated timeline, and whether subscriber net adds turn positive in the next 1–2 quarters — both are forward observations, not currently in the data pool.
- What would change the earnings verdict: see Section 7.
- Forensic tags: `06_earnings-quality` explicitly did NOT emit RF-EQ-001 (rising accruals divergent from cash earnings) or RF-EQ-002 (cash-conversion breakdown) — only 1 of 6 accrual-quality flags triggered, below the 2-flag threshold, and cash conversion never approached the "healthy" line let alone the red-flag line. No forensic tag to propagate here.

## 9. Simple Summary

- Revenue is growing (+11.37% last quarter) but slowing every year, and almost all of it now comes from raising prices — the number of paying customers is flat to shrinking.
- Margins look good right now (35.35% EBITDA margin) mainly because management has deliberately cut back on customer-acquisition spending — management itself says this won't last more than "2, 3" more quarters.
- Earnings are not fully clean: about 30–40% of reported profit and per-share earnings comes from gains on a large investment portfolio, not from the core marketplace business — real money, but volatile and unrelated to operations.
- The Street's bar is roughly fair for revenue but the earnings-per-share number for next year looks set too high, because it seems to assume those investment gains keep recurring.
- Next quarter's setup is being called "balanced," but there's a real risk the margin boost and the customer decline are actually the same underlying weakness showing up twice — if so, both could disappoint at once.
- Cash generation is genuinely strong and has been for years — the company collects cash from customers before it recognizes the revenue, and that has never reversed.
- Earnings volatility is high — several single variables (discretionary spending, investment-portfolio swings) can each move earnings by 20%+ in a year.
- This module is useful: the data is complete and current, but the master synthesizer should treat the "balanced" and "fair" framings with real caution given the compounding-risk flag.

# Historical Financials — INDIAMART

**Jurisdiction / regime:** India, listed on NSE (INDIAMART) and BSE (542726). Reporting standard: Ind AS (Indian Accounting Standards, Companies Act 2013 Sec. 133). Reporting currency: INR. Fiscal year ends **March 31** (e.g. "FY26" = year ended 31-Mar-2026). All figures below are in **₹ millions** (Capital IQ's reporting unit for this export) unless stated otherwise. Consolidated basis throughout.

Note on sourcing: the pool contains no `ciq_facts.json` sidecar for this run, so all figures below are this agent's own sourced read of the Capital IQ (CIQ) financial-statement exports and the underlying SEBI-filed annual/interim reports, cross-checked against each other. Capital IQ exports are Tier-5 evidence (CLAUDE.md §4); where a figure was independently verified against the primary filing text, that filing is cited directly.

IndiaMART reports a single set of Ind AS consolidated figures with no management-adjusted non-GAAP overlay.

Note: the Capital IQ workbook does carry its own vendor-constructed "Normalized Net Income" / "Normalized EPS" lines (e.g. Normalized Diluted EPS FY26 = ₹47.01 vs reported Diluted EPS ₹78.77) [Capital IQ export, `Financials (1).xls`, Income Statement tab]. **No quarter triggers the >30% or <20% revenue-share flag** — the mildest seasonality pattern visible is Q1 consistently the smallest quarter (~23.7–23.9% of annual revenue in all 3 years) and Q4 consistently the largest (~25.6–26.3%), a spread of roughly 2–3 percentage points. This is a modest, not material, seasonal skew — consistent with a subscription/renewal-driven B2B model rather than a sharply seasonal one. EBITDA margin, by contrast, shows a much larger year-to-year step (FY24's ~27–28% band vs FY25's ~35–39% band vs FY26's ~33–36% band) than quarter-to-quarter within a year — the variance is mostly a **year effect** (see Section 6), not a **quarter effect**.

## 6. Key Trend Summary

Revenue growth is **decelerating**: annual growth ran 30.78% (FY23) → 21.45% (FY24) → 16.01% (FY25) → 13.02% (FY26), and the latest TTM figure (+12.75%) and the most recent quarter (Q1 FY27 +11.37% YoY, the softest of the last 8 quarters) both confirm the deceleration is continuing into FY27, not just a FY23 base-effect artifact [Capital IQ export, Financials (1).xls; Surprise tab]. Margins are **volatile rather than trending in one direction**: EBITDA margin collapsed from 39.4% (FY22, a pandemic-era high) to 26.6% (FY23, −1,286 bps) as the company stepped up spending (management guided to a "28% to 29% EBITDA margins in FY24" range on the Q4 FY23 call [`IndiaMART InterMESH Limited, Q4 2023 Earnings Call, Apr 28, 2023.pdf`]), then jumped back to 37.0% in FY25 (+1,048 bps) before compressing again to 33.2% in FY26 (−385 bps); the most recent 4 quarters (Q2 FY26–Q1 FY27) show margin drifting down from 33.2% to 32.8% before a Q1 FY27 tick-up to 35.4%. Reported diluted EPS is **more volatile than either revenue or EBITDA**, swinging quarter to quarter (e.g. ₹31.24 in Q3 FY26 to ₹8.33 in Q4 FY26 to ₹28.56 in Q1 FY27) because of large, lumpy gains/losses on the company's ₹30bn+ treasury book sitting below the operating line — a downstream earnings-quality read should treat EBIT/EBITDA, not EPS, as the cleaner trend indicator (Section 3). Seasonality is **modest, not material**: Q1 (Apr–Jun) is consistently the smallest revenue quarter (~23.7–23.9% of the year) and Q4 (Jan–Mar) consistently the largest (~25.6–26.3%), a 2–3 point spread that does not clear the >30%/<20% flag threshold (Section 5). The clearest inflection point in the 5-year window is the **FY22→FY23 margin step-down** (EBITDA margin −1,286 bps on a cost build-out) followed by the **FY24→FY25 margin snap-back** (+1,048 bps); both moves are larger than any single year's revenue-growth swing, meaning cost discipline / investment cycles — not the top line — have driven most of the year-to-year swings in profitability over this period. The balance sheet is a **structural net-cash position throughout** (strict-basis net cash every year from FY23 on, deepening from ₹122mn net cash in FY23 to ₹573mn in FY26; on the broad basis that also nets the ₹30bn+ treasury book, net cash exceeds ₹30bn in FY26), so leverage is not a constraint on this business in any of the last 5 years.

## earnings / 02_revenue-drivers.md

_Source: `earnings/02_revenue-drivers.md`_

# Revenue Drivers — INDIAMART

**Jurisdiction / currency / standard:** India (NSE: INDIAMART, BSE: 542726), Ind AS, consolidated, INR. Fiscal year ends 31 March. "Q1 FY27" = quarter ended 30-Jun-2026, the most recent reported quarter as of this run (filed 21-Jul-2026). Figures below are quoted in ₹ crore (1 crore = ₹10 million) where that is how management stated them on the earnings call, and in ₹ million where sourced from the Capital IQ / filing exports used in `01_historical-financials.md` — both units are labelled inline every time.

---

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

Segment decomposition applied — 2 segments from business-model module (`analyses/INDIAMART_2026-08-13/business-model/03_segment-map.md`).

The Web and related Services segment cleared the module's own >85% single-segment revenue threshold in FY26 (91.96% of consolidated revenue [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32]), and `03_segment-map.md` itself reads the company as "best read as a single-segment business... not a genuinely multi-segment company." This report keeps the second segment (Accounting Software Services, Busy Infotech + Livekeeping) broken out anyway, because although it is only 8.04% of FY26 revenue, it supplied roughly a third of the *incremental* growth in the most recent quarter (Section 6) — a revenue-share test alone would hide that. Both segments are covered in Section 5.

---

## 2. Revenue Driver Tree

| Business Type | Revenue Formula |
|---|---|
| Subscription (Web and related Services, ~92% of revenue) | Paying suppliers × ARPU (Average Revenue Per User) |
| Subscription / software licence (Accounting Software Services, ~8% of revenue) | Licences sold / billing accounts × realized price per licence |
| Multi-segment | Sum of the two segment formulas above |

**Company-specific formula:** Consolidated revenue ≈ (paying suppliers on the IndiaMART marketplace × ARPU) + (Busy Infotech / Livekeeping licence base × price per licence and add-on take-rate), where "ARPU" is the company's own defined metric — revenue from operations for the year ÷ paying subscription suppliers at year-end [FY26 Annual Report, p.82–83].

---

## 3. Market / Share / Price / Mix Split

| Driver Bucket | Current Direction | Evidence | Importance /100 |
|---|---|---|---:|
| End-market demand | Mixed — large, growing addressable market on paper; management describes the immediate demand environment as weak | India has 79.4 million Udyam-registered enterprises as of FY26, up from 7.9 million in FY22, against IndiaMART's 220,000 paying suppliers and ~8.7 million registered (mostly free-tier) suppliers — a low-penetration, structurally growing base [FY26 Integrated Annual Report, MD&A, Udyam chart]. But in the same period management says "SMEs are really going through a lot of pain right now" [Q4 FY26 Earnings Call, Apr 30, 2026] and unique business inquiries fell from 29 million (Q1 FY26) to 26 million (Q1 FY27), roughly −10% to −11% YoY per an analyst's figure management did not dispute [Q1 FY26 Earnings Call, Jul 18, 2025: "unique business inquiries were 29 million... representing a year-on-year growth of about 17%"; Q1 FY27 Earnings Call, Jul 21, 2026: "unique business inquiries were 26 million" and Samarth Patel, Equirus: "unique business inquiry sort of declined 11%," not corrected by management] | 70 |

**Reconciliation to Section 6's Total row (Q1 FY27):** 0.0pp (volume) + 7.89pp (Web price) + 3.48pp (Accounting Software, undifferentiated) = 11.37pp reconciled, **0.0pp residual** against the stated 11.37% total. This is an unusually clean reconciliation because the two segment revenue figures sum exactly to the reported consolidated total by construction (they are the filing's own segment note, not an estimate) — the only place an assumption enters is inside the Accounting Software segment's own internal split, which is explicitly left undifferentiated above rather than modelled.

**Reconciliation to Section 6's Total row (FY26 annual):** 8.84pp (Web, itself split 1.38pp volume + 7.81pp price via the multiplicative identity revenue = subscribers × ARPU, which the company's own ARPU definition makes an identity, not a modelled ratio) + 4.17pp (Accounting Software, undifferentiated) = 13.01pp reconciled, **0.01pp residual** (rounding only, from ARPU and subscriber counts being disclosed rounded to the nearest thousand).

Because the residual is ~0 in both periods, Section 7's single-biggest-driver claim below rests on a decomposition that is fully explained, not a bridge with a large unexplained gap.

## 7. The Single Biggest Revenue Driver

**Paying-subscriber net additions to the Web segment (volume)** is the single variable most likely to move revenue over the next 3–12 months — not ARPU, even though ARPU has done all the realized growth work in the last two reported periods (Section 6a). The reasoning: in the revenue identity (subscribers × ARPU), a 10–20% move in either factor produces an equivalent percentage move in Web segment revenue, so the two drivers have identical mechanical leverage. What separates them is volatility and current trajectory. ARPU has grown ~8% every year for four straight years with no reversal in the data [FY26 Annual Report, p.83] — it is the stable half of the equation. Subscriber net adds, by contrast, swung from +2,800 (Q2 FY26) to −1,850 (Q1 FY27) within the same fiscal year, have been negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters, and management has explicitly declined to guide on when net adds turn positive again: *"we'll continue to have no guidance on the net adds until we have multiple quarters of continual success"* [Q4 FY26 Earnings Call, Apr 30, 2026]. A continuation of negative net adds shrinks the base ARPU is multiplied against and, per management's own framing, risks the price increase becoming counter-productive if churn keeps rising in response — *"if the customers are not renewing, acquiring same customer with double the intensity will make the CAC go higher and the LTV go lower"* [Q1 FY27 Earnings Call, Jul 21, 2026]. The direction today is negative (flat YoY subscriber count, accelerating quarterly net losses through Q1 FY27), and the swing factors behind it — Silver-tier gross adds/churn, the war-related and OTP-verification-related buyer declines, and the still-unresolved SME "pain" management cites — are all outside the company's full control (`10_external-dependency.md`, Section 5, independently names "Consumer cycle" / SME sentiment as its own single biggest lever, which this agent's read agrees with).

**Cycle position (Cycle-Position Rule):** the latest reported quarter is **not** a demand peak. Evidence: consolidated revenue growth has decelerated every year from +30.78% (FY23) to +13.02% (FY26) to +11.37% (Q1 FY27, the softest of the last 8 quarters per `01_historical-financials.md` Section 3); consolidated collection-from-customers growth has decelerated from +17% YoY (Q1 FY26) to +8% YoY (Q1 FY27) [Q1 FY26 and Q1 FY27 Earnings Calls]; and net subscriber adds have been negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters. This reads as a soft-patch / decelerating phase, not a trough (the company remains profitable and cash-generative — see `01_historical-financials.md` Section 1) and not a peak. Two items must be treated as non-run-rate: (1) the FY25 EBITDA-margin snap-back (+1,048bps) reflected cost discipline, not a demand re-acceleration, per `01_historical-financials.md` Section 6, so FY25's margin should not be read as the operating baseline; (2) the government MSME/GST tailwind management cites in the FY26 MD&A is a stated, forward-looking claim not yet visible in the subscriber or inquiry data this quarter (Section 4) — it must not be treated as already embedded in the current run-rate.

# Margin Drivers — INDIAMART

**Sector overlay applied (analog, per business-model `02_business-identity` §3a — a judgment call, not a literal type match):** SaaS / subscription-software margin grammar. IndiaMART's Ind AS profit & loss is a single-step statement with no cost-of-revenue / gross-profit line (confirmed by full-text search of the FY26 Annual Report — no matches for "gross profit" or "cost of revenue" [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, footnote 2]), so the SaaS overlay's headline "GAAP vs non-GAAP gross-margin gap" concept does not apply here — there is no gross-margin line to charge SBC against. The overlay concepts that DO apply and drive this report: stock-based comp as % of revenue, customer-acquisition/servicing cost as the primary opex-leverage metric (there is no raw-material, freight, or energy cost line — confirmed in business-model `06_value-chain.md` §2: "no commodity or raw-material input... it does not itself ship physical goods"), and Deferred Revenue as the RPO-analog leading indicator. The generic Cost Stack table (Section 2) is therefore built from IndiaMART's own disclosed cost lines (Employee benefits, Other expenses sub-lines), not a raw-material/freight/SG&A table, consistent with the overlay's intent.

## 1. Segment Decomposition Status

Web and related Services (the core marketplace) is 91.96% of FY26 consolidated revenue [FY26 Annual Report (Ind AS), Note 32 — Segment information] — it clears the >85% single-segment threshold in `MODULE_RULES.md`. Despite that, this agent decomposes anyway: segment-level P&L **is** disclosed for both segments (Note 32), and the second segment (Accounting Software Services, Busy Infotech + Livekeeping, 8.04% of revenue) has a large, quantifiable, disclosed margin story — its segment loss narrowed from −17.47% to −2.23% margin YoY, and its growing revenue share is itself a measurable drag on the consolidated blend (Section 7a). Standalone entity has no segment disclosure of its own ("the Company has disclosed the segment information only as part of consolidated financial statements" [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32, Standalone Financial Statements]) — the standalone P&L is, for practical purposes, the core marketplace segment, and its own voluntary "function-wise results" note (Note 34) is used below as the cleanest, fully-reconciled cost breakdown for that segment.

## 2. Cost Stack

IndiaMART has no COGS / raw-material / freight / energy line — confirmed absent in both the P&L structure and `06_value-chain.md` §2 ("no commodity or raw-material input... no freight-cost line or logistics-rate risk is disclosed"). The two EBITDA-level cost lines in the audited consolidated P&L are Employee benefits expense and Other expenses; there is no separate line for R&D (embedded in "Technology and Content Expenses" per Note 34) or SG&A (split across Selling & Distribution, Marketing, and G&A per Note 34). Figures are FY26 vs FY25, consolidated, computed and verified via an executed Python snippet (Bash) from the audited P&L notes.

**Goodwill note (not a current cost-stack item, but a tail risk to D&A/impairment):** ₹4,122.34mn (Busy Infotech) + ₹420.38mn (Livekeeping) = ₹4,542.72mn of goodwill sits on the consolidated balance sheet, and the FY26 statutory auditor (B S R & Co. LLP) named goodwill impairment a Key Audit Matter requiring judgement on revenue-growth, terminal-growth and WACC assumptions [`03_segment-map.md` §1, citing FY26 Annual Report, Independent Auditor's Report]. An impairment charge would land inside the "Depreciation, amortisation and impairment expense" line (Note 23's own title) and would hit EBITDA margin directly, not just EBIT — unlike most companies' impairment treatment. Not currently triggered; flagged as a risk, not a driver.

## 3. Gross Margin → EBITDA Margin → EBIT Margin Walk

No gross-margin concept exists for this business (no COGS line — see Section 2 preamble). The walk below uses the company's own audited "EBITDA Margin ratio" (Note 8-referenced, in the Ind AS-mandated ratio-disclosure note) as the primary figure, cross-checked against the CIQ-sourced figure already used in `01_historical-financials.md` §1 (a ~3bps gap exists between the two, consistent with the CIQ-internal reconciliation inconsistency already flagged in that report's footnote 7 — not a new gap introduced here).

| EBITDA margin (CIQ-sourced, consolidated — cross-check) | 33.18% | 37.03% | −385 | Same drivers; ~3bps gap vs company figure is a pre-existing CIQ-internal inconsistency, not newly introduced | [`01_historical-financials.md` §1, §2 footnote 7] |
| EBIT margin (consolidated) | 31.97% | 35.45% | −349 | Same EBITDA-level drivers, partially offset by a 56bps favorable D&A decline (Note 23) | [`01_historical-financials.md` §1] |

Pass-through lag: not applicable in the traditional input-cost sense (no commodity/raw-material input to pass through — `06_value-chain.md` §2). The nearest analog is customer-facing price realization on the Silver subscription tier, where management raised prices at the end of Q2 FY26 and, by Q4 FY26, attributed 1,000–1,500 of a ~3,000-supplier quarterly net-add shortfall directly to that price increase [`06_value-chain.md` §3, citing Q4 FY26 transcript] — pricing action shows up with roughly a 1–2 quarter lag in supplier churn/net-adds, not in the cost stack.

## 4. Margin Walk — Which Margin Level Matters Most?

EBITDA margin is the most useful level for this business. There is no gross margin to track (Section 3), D&A is small and mostly amortisation of the Busy Infotech/Livekeeping intangibles rather than a real economic charge on the core marketplace (asset-light, near-zero capex — ₹70mn FY26 per `01_historical-financials.md` §1), and Finance costs are structurally negligible (lease-only, Total Debt/EBITDA ~0.04x). EBITDA is also what management itself reports and discusses on every call ("Consolidated EBITDA was INR 146 crores for the quarter, representing margin of 35%" [Q1 FY27 transcript, prepared remarks, CFO Jitin Diwan]) — it is the number the company, not just this agent, treats as the operating profitability metric.

| Customer support / trust-&-verification cost buildout (KYC, OTP, buy-lead verification, agentic call handling) | Raises Other expenses ratio | Headwind | High (+191bps FY26; +168bps YoY again in Q1 FY27 — still running) | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 24; Q1 FY27 transcript, prepared remarks re: seller/buyer verification, agentic call center] |
| Buyer-acquisition digital marketing spend (Advertisement expenses) | Raises Other expenses ratio | Headwind, but decelerating | High in FY26 (+175bps); Low in Q1 FY27 (+19bps YoY — growth has slowed) | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 24; Q1 FY27/Q3 FY26 transcripts] |
| Outsourced sales cost (customer-acquisition spend) — currently pulled back | Currently a margin tailwind; reversible | Tailwind now / Headwind risk later | High (−56bps FY26; −86bps YoY in Q1 FY27) | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 24; Q1 FY27 transcript, CFO: "Margins continue to be elevated on account of savings arising from lower customer acquisition"] |

## 6. Margin Drivers By Segment

### Segment: Web and related Services (91.96% of FY26 revenue)

Segment margin fell from 40.50% (FY25) to 36.93% (FY26), a −357bps decline [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32]. Because the standalone entity is, for practical purposes, this segment (standalone revenue ₹14,428.03mn vs segment revenue ₹14,429.94mn — a ₹1.91mn gap, immaterial), the standalone functional P&L (Note 34) is used as the driver breakdown, and it reconciles almost exactly to the standalone entity's own −283.7bps EBITDA-margin change (a smaller number than the segment's raw −357bps, because Note 32's segment scope and Note 34's standalone-entity scope are not identical bases — both are audited but drawn from different notes; the gap is flagged, not resolved, per the Driver Attribution rule).

| Driver | Impact | Direction | Magnitude | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Marketing Expenses (digital buyer-acquisition ads) | +166.5bps of standalone EBITDA-margin change | Headwind | High | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 34] |
| Customer service cost (incl. RFQ/buy-lead verification) | +82.1bps | Headwind | High | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 34] |
| Selling & Distribution Expenses | +51.9bps | Headwind | Mid | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 34] |
| Technology and Content Expenses | +42.7bps | Headwind | Mid | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 34] |
| General and Administrative Expenses | −59.5bps | Tailwind (leverage) | Mid | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 34] |

### Segment: Accounting Software Services (8.04% of FY26 revenue — Busy Infotech + Livekeeping)

Segment result improved from a loss of ₹(119.16)mn (−17.47% margin) in FY25 to a loss of ₹(28.15)mn (−2.23% margin) in FY26 on revenue that nearly doubled (₹681.91mn → ₹1,261.04mn, +84.9%) [FY26 Annual Report, Note 32]. This is a genuine, quantifiable margin tailwind at the segment level — driven by billing/license growth (Busy billed ~₹59 crore in Q1 FY27 vs ~₹10 crore a year earlier per management commentary [`03_segment-map.md` §1, citing Q1 FY27 transcript]) scaling faster than the segment's cost base, plus the recent "Busy Magic" product relaunch. But because the segment is still loss-making and its revenue share nearly doubled (4.91% → 8.04% of consolidated revenue), its growing weight in the blend is a net drag on the CONSOLIDATED margin even as its own trajectory improves — this is the mix effect quantified in Section 7a. Segment-level cost-line detail (employee cost vs other cost split) is not disclosed at this granularity; the improvement is described only at the segment-result level.

All figures computed and verified via an executed Python snippet (Bash) from Notes 21, 22, 23, 24, 34, 38.

| **Total margin change (sum of Volume/opleverage + Input costs + One-offs + Other; excludes the Mix memo line)** | **−387.5** | Reconciles to the company's own −388bps EBITDA-margin-ratio change (Note 8) to within 0.5bps |

**Mix-line caveat:** the −122.4bps Mix figure is measured on a segment-revenue-weight basis (Note 32), a different basis from the P&L-line-ratio basis (Notes 21/24) used for every other row in this table. It is shown as a complementary cross-check (Section 7a), not summed into the Total, to avoid double-counting the Accounting Software Services segment's costs (which are already embedded inside the consolidated Employee-benefits and Other-expenses totals used above). Applying a segment-weight-shift figure inside a P&L-line-ratio total would be exactly the basis-mismatch error the Driver Attribution rule prohibits.

Given the reconciliation above clears essentially the full amount (99.9%+), Section 8's single-biggest-driver claim below rests on arithmetic that is fully, not partially, explained.

## 8. The Single Biggest Margin Driver

Looking forward — the question this report exists to answer — the single biggest margin driver is **management's own choice on customer-acquisition spend** (Outsourced sales cost + the digital marketing budget), not a market or input-cost force outside the company's control. The evidence: FY26's margin compression was driven roughly 78% by the Other-expenses line (Section 7a), inside which Customer support (+191bps) and Advertisement (+175bps) were the two largest single items — both discretionary. Then, in Q1 FY27, management explicitly reversed course on part of that spend: the CFO stated "margins continue to be elevated on account of savings arising from lower customer acquisition and operating leverage" [Q1 FY27 transcript, prepared remarks], and the numbers confirm it — Outsourced sales cost fell −86bps YoY in the quarter (vs −56bps for the full FY26 year, i.e., the pullback accelerated), while Customer support (+168bps) and Internet/online costs (+118bps) kept rising, meaning the pullback was selective, not a broad-based cost cut. Management has also stated it is deliberately not "pressing the growth pedal" on supplier acquisition for "2, 3 more quarters" while it works through Silver-tier churn [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2, citing Q1 FY27 transcript]. This makes the current Q1 FY27 margin level (35.35% EBITDA margin) a policy choice, not a new run-rate: the direction today is favorable (margin expanding QoQ off the FY26 trough), but the single biggest reversal risk is management resuming the outsourced-sales/marketing spend it has throttled — a budgeted ~₹10 crore/quarter digital-marketing spend was cited on the Q3 FY26 call as the target run-rate, above where actual spend has been running [Q3 FY26 transcript, Q&A].

## 9. Investment Spend — Both Signs

Capex itself is trivial for this business (₹70mn FY26, declining YoY [`01_historical-financials.md` §1]) and shows no wave to evaluate. The relevant "spend running well above its own history" is discretionary OPEX: Advertisement expenses grew +499% YoY in FY26 (₹56.64mn → ₹339.13mn, standalone Marketing Expenses +320% to ₹324.58mn [FY26 Annual Report, Note 24/34]). Both signs are stated below, rather than reading this only as a cost.

| Reading | What it would show | Evidence here |
|---|---|---|
| Spend as a future COST | A discretionary opex ramp that drags EBITDA margin now, with no committed offsetting revenue | Advertisement expenses added +175bps of margin drag in FY26 alone (Section 2/7a); management's own framing on the Q3 FY26 call describes a target run-rate of "₹10 crore" per quarter, well above where actual spend has landed most quarters, i.e. an intended further ramp, not a one-off [Q3 FY26 transcript, Q&A] |
| Spend as a DEMAND signal | Evidence that the spend is buying a real, monetizable outcome — a growing, more valuable buyer base that would eventually lift ARPU/leads | Management explicitly ties the ad spend to "shifted the buyer base... to the more higher ARPU buyers... the categories where we are able to monetize" [Q1 FY27 transcript, Q&A, CEO Dinesh Agarwal]; Deferred Revenue (the closest RPO analog) grew faster than recognised revenue in FY26 (+14% standalone vs +9% recognised revenue [`02_business-identity.md` §4]), a genuine leading indicator, though not one specifically tied to this ad spend |

**Current read: the evidence favours the COST reading, not yet the demand reading.** The volume metric management itself uses to judge the buyer-acquisition funnel — unique business inquiries — has been flat to declining through the exact period of the ad-spend ramp: 29mn (Q1 FY26) → 31mn (Q2 FY26) → 28mn (Q3 FY26) → ~27mn, described by management as a 1% decline (Q4 FY26) → 26mn (Q1 FY27) [Q1–Q4 FY26 and Q1 FY27 transcripts, prepared remarks]. An analyst asked management directly on the Q4 FY26 call: "despite of us investing so much on performance marketing, why this number is not inching up?" [Q4 FY26 transcript, Q&A] — management's answer pointed to mix/quality effects (shifting spend toward higher-ARPU categories) rather than disputing the flat volume trend. The observable that would flip this read: a sustained rise in unique business inquiries and/or in paying-supplier net-additions attributable to the higher-ARPU categories the ad spend targets — not yet visible across the four quarters of data available in this pool. Until that shows up, the ad-spend ramp reads as a margin cost with an unproven payoff, not a demand signal comparable to a backlog or bookings figure.

## Cycle-Position Read (Cyclicality — MODULE_RULES Hard Rule)

`10_external-dependency.md` flags "Consumer/SME cycle" and "Geopolitics" as High-dependency rows for this business, so a cycle-position statement is required. Consolidated EBITDA margin over the last five fiscal years ran 39.43% (FY22, described in `01_historical-financials.md` as "a pandemic-era high") → 26.57% (FY23, trough — a deliberate cost build-out) → 26.54% (FY24, trough continued) → 37.03% (FY25, a snapback close to the FY22 peak) → 33.18% (FY26, mid-range) [`01_historical-financials.md` §1]. The latest reported quarter (Q1 FY27, 35.35%) sits in the mid-to-upper part of this five-year band — above the FY23/FY24 trough and above FY26's full-year average, but below both the FY22 pandemic-era high and the FY25 peak. This is explicitly **not a normalised run-rate**: management's own words describe the current level as "elevated" because of a deliberate, temporary pullback in customer-acquisition spend while Silver-tier churn is being addressed (Section 8) — a policy choice that management has said will persist for roughly "2, 3" more quarters, not a structural cost improvement, and one that reverses the moment outsourced-sales/marketing spend resumes toward its stated ~₹10 crore/quarter target.

| EPS Normalized next FY (FY2027) | 6 | 8 | −14.3% (of 14 analysts who revised) | Last 3 months |

Revenue and EPS revision breadth both skew negative (more analysts cutting than raising), while EBITDA revision breadth skews positive (more analysts raising than cutting) — analysts are trimming the top line and bottom line while raising their margin assumption, a genuinely offsetting pattern rather than a uniform "estimates rising" or "estimates falling" story. Target Price revision breadth over the same window is sharply negative (1 up / 16 down of 18 analysts, Last 3 months, `Revisions` tab, Non-Periodic Data Items) and the average sell-side recommendation has drifted from Outperform (2.11–2.44) six-to-twelve months ago to Hold (2.61) currently (`Trends` tab, Non-Periodic Trends) — corroborating that the sell-side has been de-rating the name over the past year, consistent with the estimate cuts above.

## 6. Historical Beat / Miss Pattern

Revenue and EBITDA figures are sourced from the `Surprise` tab's Fiscal Quarters section (Company Level, ₹mm); EPS Normalized actuals for FQ2 2026–FQ4 2026 and FQ1 2027 are cross-checked against the same tab. **Data-quality flag:** the Q1 FY27 transcript's own embedded CIQ summary table states FQ4 2026 (Mar-2026 quarter) actual EPS Normalized as ₹11.54 with a −52.26% surprise, while the `Surprise` tab (part of the same Estimates Report workbook, pulled 2026-08-13) states the FQ4 2026 actual as ₹8.33 with the same −52.26% surprise percentage against a different quoted estimate base. Both numbers are cited to their own document; this is flagged rather than silently reconciled — the discrepancy does not change the qualitative pattern (a large miss that quarter) but the reader should not treat ₹11.54 and ₹8.33 as interchangeable.

| Period | Revenue Beat/Miss | EPS (Normalized) Beat/Miss | Magnitude | Notes |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| Q2 FY26 (Sep-2025) | Beat | Miss | Rev +1.33% / EPS −35.1% | Revenue: Actual ₹3,910mm vs Est. ₹3,858.8mm. EPS: Actual ₹13.71 vs Est. ₹23.30 (per transcript's own mini-table) |
| Q3 FY26 (Dec-2025) | Beat | Beat | Rev +1.14% / EPS +55.6%–+36.8%* | Revenue: Actual ₹4,016mm vs Est. ₹3,970.8mm. EPS: Actual ₹31.24 vs Est. ₹25.00 (transcript) / ₹20.075 (Surprise tab, differing bases — *both cited sources agree it was a large beat, magnitude differs 36.8% vs 55.6%) |
| Q4 FY26 (Mar-2026) | Beat | Miss | Rev +0.33% / EPS −52.3% | Revenue: Actual ₹4,043mm vs Est. ₹4,029.6mm. EPS: Actual ₹8.33 (Surprise tab) / ₹11.54 (transcript mini-table) vs Est. ₹17.45–21.30 — see data-quality flag above |
| Q1 FY27 (Jun-2026) | In-line | Beat | Rev 0.0% / EPS +27.8% (transcript) or +33.1% (Surprise tab) | Revenue: Actual ₹4,144mm = Est. ₹4,144mm (transcript shows the same rounded figures but states a −0.66% surprise — a rounding artefact in the extract, flagged not resolved). EPS: Actual ₹28.56 vs Est. ₹22.85 (transcript) — management attributes a large share of the beat to a ₹107cr other-income mark-to-market gain on the treasury portfolio (`Q1 FY27 transcript, prepared remarks`), not core operating performance |

**The pattern that matters for the bar:** revenue surprises have been small and consistently positive (0% to +1.3%) across all four of the last quarters — the Street's revenue estimation has been tightly calibrated. EPS surprises over the same four quarters have swung wildly (roughly −35%, +37%–+56%, −52%, +28%–+33%) — and management's own Q1 FY27 disclosure that ₹107cr of other income came from treasury mark-to-market gains indicates the EPS volatility is substantially a below-the-line (non-operating) phenomenon, not a sign that the operating "bar" itself is mis-set.

## 7. Bar Assessment

**Bar is fair.**

The evidence points in different directions depending on the metric and horizon, and none dominates cleanly enough to call the bar low or high overall. Revenue: FY2027 consensus (₹1,720.19cr, +9.6% YoY) has been essentially flat over the last quarter (−0.9% vs 90 days ago) after a full year of cuts (−3.1% vs 12 months ago), and the historical beat/miss record shows the revenue line has been consistently, tightly in-line (0% to +1.3% surprise) for four straight quarters — a well-calibrated, not obviously low, bar. EBITDA/EBIT revision breadth is net positive (+28.6% over the last three months) even as the FY2027 EBITDA number sits 4.5% below where it was 12 months ago — margin expectations are being nudged back up from a lower base, roughly balancing out. EPS is the most mixed: the FY2027 number ticked up slightly in the last quarter (+0.8%) reversing part of a 12-month, −7.3% cut, but the *next-quarter* (FQ2 FY27) EPS estimate was cut −5.5% in the same window — notably, this cut came *after* Q1 FY27's large reported EPS beat, because the Street explicitly did not extrapolate the one-off treasury mark-to-market gain that drove that beat (Section 6). Revenue and EBITDA breadth for the next quarter both rose modestly post-print (+1.7% and an implied margin uptick), so the operating-line bar for the next quarter is, if anything, slightly higher, while the EPS-specific bar for the next quarter is lower — genuinely offsetting signals within the same reporting period, not noise. Layered on top: sell-side sentiment (target price −21% over six months, recommendation drifting from Outperform to Hold) has de-rated the stock alongside the estimate cuts, and management's own supplier-churn commentary points to continued near-term core-KPI softness for "2, 3 quarters" — a headwind the Street appears to already be pricing given the flattened (not rising) revenue estimates. No formal numeric guidance exists to anchor a guidance-vs-consensus gap (Section 3), so this call rests entirely on revision momentum and historical beat/miss behaviour.

# Beat / Miss Setup — INDIAMART

## 1. Next Quarter Context

The next quarter to report is Q2 FY27 (July–September 2026), expected around 21-Oct-2026, following the Q1 FY27 print (June quarter, reported 21-Jul-2026) [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §1]. IndiaMART gives no formal numeric guidance, so the bar is set entirely by sell-side consensus: revenue ₹4,222.5mn (₹422.25cr), up +1.67% in the last month, and normalized EPS ₹20.23, cut −5.47% in the last month — a cut that came *after* Q1 FY27's reported EPS beat, because analysts did not carry forward the one-off treasury gain that drove it [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4, §6]. `04_guidance-consensus.md` calls the overall bar "fair" — not obviously low or high — because revenue and EBITDA revision trends are mildly positive while EPS and target-price revisions are mildly negative [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §7].

## 2. Beat Scenarios

| Scenario | Driver | What Would Need To Happen | Likelihood (High / Mid / Low) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARPU keeps compounding while net adds stabilize | ARPU / price realization (Web segment) | ARPU (revenue per paying supplier) continues its four-year run of ~8% annual growth, and paying-supplier net adds stop shrinking (even flat, not necessarily positive) | Mid | ARPU rose from ₹61,000 to ₹66,000 in FY26, +8.2%, "the fourth straight year of ~8-9% ARPU growth," with management stating growth was "primarily driven by improvement in realization" [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §3, §7]. This alone accounted for +7.89pp of the +11.37% Q1 FY27 revenue growth [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §6] |
| Cost pullback runs longer than the stated 2-3 quarters | Discretionary customer-acquisition spend (Outsourced sales cost, digital marketing) | Management continues holding back on Outsourced sales cost and marketing spend beyond the "2, 3 more quarters" it flagged, keeping EBITDA margin near the Q1 FY27 "elevated" 35.35% level rather than reverting toward FY26's 33.18% average | Mid | CFO: "margins continue to be elevated on account of savings arising from lower customer acquisition and operating leverage" [`03_margin-drivers.md` §8]; Outsourced sales cost fell −86bps YoY in Q1 FY27, an acceleration from FY26's −56bps [`03_margin-drivers.md` §5, §8]; EBITDA revision breadth for FY2027 is net +28.6% (9 up / 5 down of 14 analysts) even as revenue and EPS breadth skew negative [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §5] |
| Accounting Software segment (Busy/Livekeeping) keeps accelerating | Segment revenue growth (8% of consolidated revenue but a rising share) | Busy license growth reaches the "15% to 20%" range management flagged (up from ~10%/year trailing) as the subscription migration continues, and billing growth holds nearer its "normalized" 30-40% range | Mid | Segment revenue recognized grew +49.4% YoY in Q1 FY27, contributing +3.48pp of the +11.37% consolidated growth despite being only 8% of revenue [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §5, §6]; management guided "15% to 20%" license growth for "the immediate year or 2" [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2] |
| GST/Udyam formalization tailwind starts showing in the data | End-market demand (Udyam-registered universe) | The GST rate cuts and MSME-formalization trend management cites in the FY26 MD&A begin to show up as improved unique-business-inquiry or paying-supplier trends this quarter, rather than remaining a forward claim | Low | Management calls this an expected future "consumption boost" [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §4] but the same-period transcripts describe SME "pain," and unique business inquiries fell ~10-11% YoY through Q1 FY27 with no sign of this tailwind yet visible [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §3-4] |

## 4. What Magnitude Matters?

| Metric | Consensus / Bar | Material Beat Threshold | Material Miss Threshold | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Revenue | ₹4,222.5mn (₹422.25cr), next Q [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4] | >+2% (≳₹4,307mn) | <−1.5% (≲₹4,159mn) | Revenue surprises have been tightly calibrated for four straight quarters (0% to +1.3%, one quarter exactly in-line) [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6] — a move outside that narrow historical band would be a genuine surprise, not noise |
| EBITDA / EBIT | No quarterly EBITDA consensus disclosed in the pool (only FY2027 annual: ₹5,828.73mn / ₹582.87cr, implying a 33.9% margin) [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §3] | Quarterly EBITDA margin sustained above ~35% (i.e., Q1 FY27's "elevated" level holds) | Quarterly EBITDA margin reverting to the FY26 full-year average of 33.18% or below | EBITDA revision breadth is net +28.6% even as the FY2027 number sits 4.5% below where it stood 12 months ago [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4-5]; margin is currently a discretionary-spend policy choice, not a structural level [`03_margin-drivers.md` §8] |
| EPS | ₹20.23 normalized, next Q, cut −5.47% in the last month [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §4] | Any beat NOT explained by a large non-operating treasury gain | Any miss driven by the absence of a prior-quarter-sized treasury gain, read in isolation | Quarterly EPS surprises have swung from −52% to +56% over the last four quarters, "substantially a below-the-line (non-operating) phenomenon" [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6] — an EPS beat or miss number on its own is close to meaningless here without separating the treasury-book swing from the operating result |
| Guidance | None issued — no formal point or range guidance for revenue, EBITDA or EPS [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §2] | N/A | N/A | Cannot define a guidance-vs-consensus gap without a guidance baseline; the only forward-looking company statements are qualitative (Section 5) |

## 5. In-Line Print But Bad Guidance Risk

| Risk | Evidence | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| In-line current quarter but management extends the churn-resolution timeline | Management has already declined to give a net-add timeline "until we have multiple quarters of continual success" and separately said it expects the current supplier decline to persist for "2, 3 more quarters" [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §7; `04_guidance-consensus.md` §2] | Since there is no formal numeric guidance, this qualitative timeline IS the guidance. If it slips further out on the call, that is functionally a guide-down even with in-line reported numbers |
| Beat current quarter EBITDA but management signals resuming acquisition spend | The Q3 FY26 call named a target run-rate of "₹10 crore" per quarter in digital marketing, above where actual spend has run most quarters — i.e., a stated intent to ramp further [`03_margin-drivers.md` §9] | A margin beat driven by deferred spend, paired with commentary that the spend is about to resume, would be a weaker signal than the headline number suggests |
| Beat EPS due to treasury gains, miss on operating quality | Management itself attributed "a large share" of the Q1 FY27 EPS beat to a ₹107cr other-income mark-to-market gain on the treasury book, not core operating performance [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6] | An EPS beat built on a non-operating, volatile line (swings of −52% to +56% surprise in the last four quarters) does not confirm operating strength; EBIT/EBITDA are the cleaner reads [`01_historical-financials.md` §3, §6] |
| Beat revenue but the underlying volume base keeps shrinking | Paying-subscriber net adds have been negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters even as ARPU-driven revenue growth continues; unique business inquiries fell ~10-11% YoY through Q1 FY27 [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §4, §7] | Revenue can beat this quarter purely on price while the customer base that revenue is billed against keeps eroding — a leading indicator for weaker growth several quarters out, not visible in the current headline print |

## 6. Seasonality Read

Seasonality neither helps nor hurts the setup meaningfully. Q2 (Jul–Sep), the quarter about to report, has averaged 24.86% of annual revenue across FY24-FY26 — squarely in the middle of the four quarters, below Q4's 25.88% but above Q1's 23.71%, a spread of only ~2 percentage points that `01_historical-financials.md` explicitly says does not clear its >30%/<20% seasonality flag [`01_historical-financials.md` §5]. Quarterly EBITDA margin for Q2 has swung far more year to year than quarter to quarter within a year (27.15% in FY24 Q2, 38.71% in FY25 Q2, 33.17% in FY26 Q2), confirming that the "year effect" (cost-cycle and spend decisions) — not the calendar quarter — is what will decide the margin outcome this time too [`01_historical-financials.md` §5-6].

## 7. Historical Pattern

IndiaMART's revenue line has beaten or matched consensus in each of the last four quarters by a tight 0% to +1.3% margin, including an exactly in-line Q1 FY27 print — this should be weighted as a real signal that the sell-side's revenue model is well calibrated, so a large revenue surprise in either direction next quarter would be unusual [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §6]. EPS, by contrast, has swung wildly (roughly −35%, +37%-+56%, −52%, +28%-+33% over the same four quarters) almost entirely because of the lumpy, non-operating treasury-gains line sitting below EBIT [`01_historical-financials.md` §3; `04_guidance-consensus.md` §6]. The synthesizer should weight the revenue pattern heavily as a base rate for the operating top line, and weight the EPS pattern lightly (or not at all) as a read on operating performance — it is closer to a coin-flip driven by treasury-book marks than a signal about the business.

## 8. Setup Verdict

**Setup is balanced.**

The single most important factor is that the two dominant near-term forces point in opposite directions and are roughly offsetting: paying-subscriber net adds have been negative in 3 of the last 4 quarters and management has given no timeline for a turn (a revenue-side drag), while EBITDA margin is currently "elevated" precisely because management has deliberately deferred customer-acquisition spend for "2, 3 more quarters" (a margin-side tailwind) [`02_revenue-drivers.md` §7; `03_margin-drivers.md` §8]. The single biggest risk that could flip this to a clear miss is if subscriber net adds deteriorate further and force management to resume acquisition spend earlier than planned to defend growth — that would turn both drivers negative at once, since the margin tailwind and the "hold off on spend" stance are the same policy choice.

## 9. Second-Quarter Look-Ahead

Visibility into the quarter after next (Q3 FY27, Oct–Dec 2026) is limited: `04_guidance-consensus.md` provides consensus only for the next quarter (FQ2 FY27) and the full FY2027 year, not FQ3 FY27 specifically [`04_guidance-consensus.md` §3-4]. The one directional signal available is that management's "2, 3 more quarters" churn-resolution and spend-pullback framing, given from the Q1 FY27 call (Jul-2026), would put the expected resolution window roughly around Q3-Q4 FY27 — meaning the margin tailwind identified in Section 8 could plausibly still be in place for Q2 FY27 but is more likely to be fading or reversing by Q3 FY27, a genuine change in setup rather than a continuation, though this is inference from management's own stated timeline, not from disclosed Q3 FY27-specific data. Inference, not from filings.

## 10. Pre-Mortem

If this balanced setup fails, the most likely reason is that the margin tailwind (deferred customer-acquisition spend) and the revenue drag (falling subscriber net adds) turned out not to be independent but to be the same underlying weakness expressing itself twice — management held spend back specifically because underlying demand was soft, and when that softness did not resolve in "2, 3 quarters," both margin and revenue missed together instead of offsetting. A secondary risk is treating a non-operating treasury-book swing as an operating EPS "beat" or "miss" when the real story sat entirely in EBIT/EBITDA.

**Lead figure is reported FCF above — it is real, bank-verified cash, not fictitious.** However, a large and *structural* (not one-off) share of the YoY growth in FCF is attributable to the growth in customer prepayments (Unearned Revenue), which is itself decelerating with the top line. Per CLAUDE.md §15, the supplementary "ex-deferred-revenue-growth" view is shown below, labelled as this agent's own construction (Inference, not from filings) — it is **not** a substitute lead figure because the deferred-revenue build is a recurring feature of the subscription model across all 5 years, not a lumpy one-off customer advance:

**Finding:** reported FCF grew every year and looks stable, but roughly half of it is the cash benefit of a growing prepayment book. Once that structural float benefit is stripped out, underlying operating FCF growth decelerated sharply from +41.5% (FY25) to +5.8% (FY26) — tracking the revenue-growth deceleration already flagged in `01_historical-financials` (30.8%→13.0% FY23→FY26), not diverging from it. This is a magnitude finding, not a manipulation finding: the prepayment cash is real and collected, but its growth rate — not its existence — is the thing to watch.

---

## 2. Cash Conversion Assessment

CFO has tracked *above* EBITDA in every one of the last 5 years (121%–182% of EBITDA), never once dipping toward the 70% "healthy" line, let alone the 50% red-flag line — so the mechanical cash-conversion-breakdown check does **not** trigger. This is structural, not a one-off: IndiaMART sells prepaid annual/multi-year subscriptions, so cash is collected up front and Unearned Revenue (₹19,652.60mn at FY26 vs ₹16,776.49mn at FY25, +17.1% YoY [FY26 Annual Report, Note 19]) keeps growing every year — it has never declined, which is the single strongest positive cash-quality signal in this dossier. The trajectory shows some volatility (182% in FY23 down to 121% in FY25, back up to 133% in FY26) but no deterioration: the ratio simply mean-reverts around a very high base as EBITDA itself swings (see `01_historical-financials` §1 on the FY23 margin step-down and FY25 snap-back). No RF-EQ-002 condition is met.

---

## 3. Working Capital Trends

IndiaMART is a subscription/services marketplace with **no inventory** ("Inventory Method: NA" [Capital IQ export, `Financials (1).xls`, Balance Sheet tab]) and **no company-disclosed COGS/cost-of-revenue line** — its Ind AS profit & loss statement is single-step (Employee benefits, Finance costs, D&A, Other expenses) [FY26 Annual Report, Consolidated Statement of Profit and Loss, p. as cited in `01_historical-financials` fn.²]. DIO is not applicable. DPO below uses CIQ's own vendor-constructed "Cost Of Goods Sold" bucket as the denominator — flagged as Tier-5 vendor construction, not a statutory line — and the disclosed Accounts Payable balance is trivial (₹13.02mn at FY26, 0.1% of Total Current Liabilities), so DPO is not a meaningful liquidity signal for this business; it is shown only because the template requires it.

| Metric | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 | Direction | Risk |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Receivable days (DSO)⁶ | 10.42 | 11.15 | 8.89 | Falling in FY26 after a mild FY25 rise | Low — trivially small in absolute terms; subscription model collects most cash upfront |
| Inventory days (DIO) | N/A | N/A | N/A | Not applicable | Not applicable — no inventory (services business) |
| Payable days (DPO)⁷ | 0.31 | 0.48 | 0.63 | Rising in % terms | Not meaningful — sub-1-day in absolute terms; AP is 0.1% of current liabilities, not a real supplier-financing signal |
| Cash conversion cycle (DSO+DIO−DPO) | 10.11 | 10.67 | 8.26 | Improving in FY26 | Low |

⁶ DSO = 365 × average Total Receivables ÷ Revenue, average of opening/closing balances. Receivables: FY23 284.30, FY24 398.78, FY25 449.39, FY26 314.86 [Capital IQ export, Balance Sheet tab].
⁷ DPO = 365 × average Accounts Payable ÷ CIQ "Cost Of Goods Sold" (vendor construction). Accounts Payable: FY23 4.25, FY24 5.03, FY25 11.18, FY26 13.02 [Capital IQ export, Balance Sheet tab]. COGS: FY24 5,506.62, FY25 6,111.19, FY26 7,016.59 [Capital IQ export, Income Statement tab].

**Flag check:** DSO rising >10% YoY? FY24→FY25 +7.0% (below threshold); FY25→FY26 −20.3% (falling). Not triggered. DIO rising >15%? Not applicable. DPO "rising sharply"? The percentage move (+56% FY24→FY25, +30% FY25→FY26) technically looks large but the absolute base is sub-1-day and the AP balance is economically immaterial (₹13mn against ₹13,650mn of current liabilities) — **not treated as a genuine liquidity signal.**

**The metric that actually matters for this business is the deferred-revenue (contract-liability) trend, not DSO/DIO/DPO.** Total Unearned Revenue (current + non-current) grew every year: FY22 ₹9,070.38mn → FY23 ₹11,624.63mn → FY24 ₹14,399.81mn → FY25 ₹16,776.49mn → FY26 ₹19,652.60mn [FY26 Annual Report, Note 19; Capital IQ Balance Sheet tab]. Operating working capital (excluding cash/investments from current assets, per `01_historical-financials` fn.⁴) is **negative** ₹12,916.52mn at FY26 — the company is effectively financed by its own customers. Deferred-revenue growth (+17.1% FY26) currently outpaces recognised-revenue growth (+13.02% FY26), a forward-looking positive: bookings are still running ahead of recognition.

---

## 4. Non-GAAP Adjustments

**None disclosed.** A full-text search of the FY26 Annual Report for "adjusted EBITDA", "non-GAAP", "adjusted EPS" and "adjusted net profit" returned no matches [`IndiaMART_InterMESH_Limited_-_Form_Annual_Report(Apr-30-2026).pdf`, full-text search, 2026-08-13 — same search already run by `01_historical-financials` §4]. IndiaMART reports a single set of Ind AS consolidated GAAP figures; there is no management-adjusted overlay for the accrual-quality checklist to test against, and consequently no exclusion game (e.g., excluding Stock-Based Compensation from an "adjusted" number) is possible — SBC is fully expensed within Employee benefits expense in the reported GAAP P&L [FY26 Annual Report, Note 21: Employee share-based payment expense ₹366.20mn FY26 vs ₹187.44mn FY25, within total Employee benefits expense ₹6,928.25mn].

| Adjustment | Amount | Recurring? (Y/N) | Concern Level (Low/Mid/High) | Evidence |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Company-disclosed non-GAAP adjustment | None found | N/A | N/A | Full-text search, FY26 Annual Report, 2026-08-25 (no matches) |
| Stock-Based Compensation (fully in GAAP earnings, not excluded from anything) | ₹366.20mn (FY26), ₹187.44mn (FY25) — **+95.4% YoY**, rising from 3.65% to 7.03% of EBITDA | Y — recurring, and growing fast | Low (fully expensed, not hidden) but worth monitoring given the growth rate | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 21] |

CIQ separately carries a "Normalized Net Income" / "Normalized Diluted EPS" line (₹47.01 vs reported ₹78.77 diluted EPS, FY26) — this is Capital IQ's own vendor normalization, **not** company-disclosed, and its precise methodology is not documented in the workbook (already flagged in `01_historical-financials` §4). Not treated as an "adjustment" for scoring purposes here; carried forward to §7 for context only.

## 5. One-Off Items (last 3 years)

| Item | Period | Amount (₹mn) | Classification | Evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Gain (Loss) On Sale Of Invest. (fair-value gain/realised gain on the ~₹30bn treasury book of mutual funds, ETFs, bonds) | FY24 / FY25 / FY26 | 2,047.16 / 2,669.22 / 1,906.51 | **Recurring "one-off"** — CIQ's own income-statement structure buckets this under "Unusual Items," but it has recurred, at material size, in every one of the last 5 years (FY22–FY26: 1,037.96 / 1,746.47 / 2,047.16 / 2,669.22 / 1,906.51) | [Capital IQ export, Income Statement tab, "Unusual Items" block; FY26 Annual Report, Note 20 "Other income" — Fair value gain (net) on mutual funds/ETFs/bonds ₹1,129.48mn + Fair value gain on Investment in other entities ₹777.03mn = ₹1,906.51mn FY26] |
| Merger & Related Restructuring Charges (Scheme of Amalgamation: Busy Infotech / Hello Trade / Tolexo) | FY23 only | −40.7 | Genuine one-off (isolated to FY23; ₹0 in FY22, FY24, FY25, FY26) | [Capital IQ export, Income Statement tab; FY26 Annual Report, Note 38 "Scheme of Amalgamation"] |
| Liabilities and provisions no longer required, written back | FY26 | +40.12 | Genuine one-off, small | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 20 "Other income"] |
| Income-tax / GST demands (Tolexo AY16-17, AY17-18; GST TRAN-1 credit dispute) | Ongoing, disclosed contingent liabilities, not yet in P&L | 302.68 (income tax) + 219.18 (GST) contingent, undiscounted | Genuine contingency — not recognised in P&L; management believes position defensible, no provision booked | [FY26 Annual Report, Note 36 "Contingent liabilities and commitments"] |
| Asset Writedown | FY24 / FY25 / FY26 | 4.82 / 0.46 / 0.16 | Genuine, immaterial | [Capital IQ export, Income Statement tab] |

**The material finding here is the first row.** The "investment gains" are legitimate under Ind AS (FVTPL fair-value-through-P&L accounting for the treasury book is mandatory, not a choice), fully disclosed in Note 20, and not fraudulent — but they are **not actually unusual**: they have appeared, at material size, in all 5 years reviewed. Labelling them "Unusual Items" (as CIQ's own income-statement structure does) is the exact "recurring one-off" trap this section exists to catch — carried into §7 and §8, and into the Section 10 finding below.

## 6. Accrual Quality Flags

| Flag | Triggered (Y/N) | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Revenue growing faster than CFO for 2+ years | **Y** (3 consecutive years) | Revenue growth FY24/25/26: 21.45% / 16.01% / 13.02%; CFO growth over the same years: 17.51% / 11.45% / 11.39% [Calc. from Capital IQ export]. **Context, not a red flag on its own:** CFO/EBITDA remains 121%–176% across these same 3 years (§2) — this reflects a *decelerating float benefit* (deferred-revenue growth cooling in line with the top line, §3), not receivables build-up or channel stuffing. |
| Receivables growing faster than revenue | N (isolated single-year exception, already reversed) | Receivables +40.3% in FY24 (vs revenue +21.45%) — the one year this triggers — but −29.9% in FY25→FY26... actually FY25 receivables +12.7% (below revenue +16.01%), and FY26 receivables −29.9% (revenue +13.02%). Only FY24 shows the pattern, and it fully reversed the following year [Capital IQ export, Balance Sheet tab]. |
| Inventory growing faster than COGS | N/A | No inventory — services business (§3). |
| Deferred revenue declining (subscription/contract business) | N | Unearned Revenue grew every year FY22–FY26 (₹9,070mn → ₹19,653mn), including +17.1% in FY26 alone, outpacing revenue growth (§3). This is the single strongest positive signal in this review. |
| Capitalized costs growing as % of revenue | N | Capex fell from 1.75% of revenue (FY23) to 0.45% (FY26); Other Intangibles balance declined every year FY22→FY26 (no fresh material capitalisation) [Capital IQ export, Balance Sheet / Cash Flow tabs]. |
| Frequent accounting policy changes | N | No change-in-accounting-policy or change-in-useful-life disclosures found in a full-text search of the FY26 Annual Report; only the routine FY25 Scheme of Amalgamation (a corporate restructuring, not a policy change) [FY26 Annual Report, Note 38]. |

**1 of 6 flags triggered — below the 2-flag threshold.** `RF-EQ-001 (rising accruals divergent from cash earnings)` is **not** emitted: cash conversion remains far above the healthy line throughout (§2), and the single triggered flag is explained by a decelerating (not reversing) structural cash source, not by classic accrual manipulation (receivables build, inventory build, or capitalized-cost inflation — all of which read N above).

## 7. Reported vs Adjusted Reconciliation

IndiaMART does **not** disclose company-defined adjusted metrics (§4). The one reconciliation the filings and CIQ workbook do support is between statutory Ind AS Profit Before Tax and CIQ's own "EBT Excl. Unusual Items" line, which strips out the recurring investment gains flagged in §5 — shown here because it directly quantifies how much of reported pre-tax profit is non-operating:

| Metric | Reported (Ind AS, statutory) FY26 | CIQ "Excl. Unusual Items" (vendor construction) FY26 | Difference | % of Reported | Recurring? | Evidence |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Profit Before Tax (PBT / EBT) | 6,479.43 | 4,532.11 | 1,947.32 | 30.1% | **Y — has recurred every year FY22–FY26 despite CIQ's "unusual" label** | [FY26 Annual Report, Consolidated Statement of P&L; Capital IQ export, Income Statement tab, "EBT Incl./Excl. Unusual Items" rows] |
| Net Income | 4,746.82 | Not separately reconciled by CIQ on a tax-effected basis | — | — | — | [FY26 Annual Report] |
| EPS (diluted) | ₹78.77 | ₹47.01 (CIQ "Normalized Diluted EPS" — vendor construction, methodology not documented) | ₹31.76 | 40.3% | Directionally consistent with the PBT gap above, but not independently verifiable from the workbook's own documentation | [Capital IQ export, Income Statement tab — same figure already flagged in `01_historical-financials` §4] |
| EBITDA / EBIT | 5,205.94 / 5,015.93 | Not applicable — EBITDA/EBIT are computed on Revenue from Operations only and already exclude the investment gains (a "Total Income" line, not "Revenue from Operations," carries them) | — | — | — | [FY26 Annual Report; Capital IQ export] |

**Reading this table:** EBIT and EBITDA are already clean of the investment-gains distortion (they sit above the "Other income" line in the Ind AS P&L structure). It is PBT, Net Income and EPS that are materially inflated by a recurring, disclosed, non-operating item — 30% of PBT and roughly 40% of diluted EPS in FY26. Use EBIT/EBITDA, not EPS, as the primary earnings-quality read for this company (consistent with `01_historical-financials` §3's own flag on EPS volatility).
